jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Enterprise Account Executive

About the Role

The litigation landscape is changing forever thanks to generative AI. We're looking for an entrepreneurial Account Executive with a strong commercial track record to join our growing team in London and help bring Wexler’s platform to litigation teams around the world.

As an Enterprise Account Executive at Wexler, you will focus on selling to legal organisations including enterprise law firms, litigation boutiques, barristers’ chambers, and specialist dispute practices across the UK, US, and other international markets. You’ll work directly with partners and senior lawyers to demonstrate how Wexler’s AI can transform document review, uncover case-winning facts, and dramatically accelerate complex disputes.

This is not a traditional transactional sales role. You’ll operate as a trusted advisor to litigation teams, developing a deep understanding of how disputes are run and helping lawyers rethink how AI can support case strategy and document-heavy investigations.

You will own the full sales cycle, from discovery through to negotiation and close, converting inbound interest and BDR-generated opportunities into long-term customers. You’ll work closely with our BDR team, who support pipeline generation and initial outreach, allowing you to focus on high-quality conversations and closing deals.

As an early member of the commercial team, you’ll also work closely with the CEO and Co-Founder to shape our go-to-market strategy, refine how we sell into the legal industry, and build the sales playbooks that will support our rapid growth.

What you'll do

You'll work directly with litigation teams exploring how AI can dramatically improve document review, fact discovery, and case strategy.

Own the full sales cycle from qualified opportunity through to negotiation and close with partners and legal decision-makers.

Convert inbound self-generated and BDR-generated opportunities into new customers, working closely with our BDRs to maintain a strong pipeline of qualified prospects.

Sell to legal organisations, including, enterprise law firms, litigation boutiques, barristers’ chambers, and specialist dispute practices across the UK, US, and international markets.

Run discovery conversations with partners and associates to understand their litigation workflows, current document review challenges, and the types of matters where Wexler can deliver the most impact.

Deliver compelling product demonstrations showing how Wexler’s AI uncovers critical case facts across large document sets.

Build strong relationships with legal decision-makers, including partners, senior associates, and innovation teams within litigation practices.

Develop expansion pathways within accounts, identifying new matters, practice groups, or offices where Wexler can deliver additional value.

Navigate commercial negotiations and procurement processes, ensuring deals close efficiently while aligning pricing with usage and value.

Collaborate closely with Product and Engineering, sharing insights from the field about litigation workflows and feature opportunities.

Partner with our Customer Success team to ensure smooth handoffs and strong early adoption after deals close.

Help refine our sales motion, contributing to messaging, pricing models, and sales processes as we scale.

What you bring

You understand that litigation AI isn’t just another software purchase — it’s a fundamental shift in how legal professionals approach their most complex disputes. You thrive on working with brilliant, demanding lawyers who expect excellence and have zero tolerance for technology that doesn’t deliver results.

We’re looking for:

3–5 years in Account Executive or Sales roles selling B2B software, ideally into professional services or legal teams.

A proven track record of closing deals with enterprise organisations, multi-stakeholder buyers and complex sales cycles.

Experience running full sales cycles, from discovery through to negotiation and close.

Strong consultative selling skills, particularly with expert users such as lawyers, consultants, or accountants.

Experience collaborating with SDR/BDR teams to convert qualified opportunities into revenue.

Commercial instinct and deal-closing ability, including building business cases and negotiating pricing.

Technical curiosity and learning agility; you can quickly understand how AI models work and translate technical capabilities into clear business value.

Executive communication skills; you’re comfortable engaging partners and senior legal stakeholders.

Startup mentality — you thrive in ambiguity and enjoy building new sales processes as the company scales.

AI enthusiasm — you’re excited about the potential of AI to transform professional services.

Nice to have: experience selling legal technology or software into law firms, litigation boutiques, or barristers’ chambers, or a background in law (e.g. law degree or legal training).

London-based and office-focused — we work from WeWork Aldwych 4 days per week, and face-to-face collaboration is core to our culture and success.

What we offer

At Wexler, you'll work with some of the world’s most sophisticated litigation teams on problems that can determine case outcomes. You’ll operate in a fast-scaling, entrepreneurial environment where your work directly impacts company growth.

As an early member of the commercial team, you’ll help define how Wexler sells into the legal industry while building relationships with the firms shaping the future of litigation.

You’ll work closely with our founding team and cross-functional partners, contributing directly to product evolution and go-to-market strategy.

We offer a competitive salary, significant equity in a rapidly growing company, huge autonomy and ownership, budget for learning and professional growth, and bi-annual team retreats.

jobs.title: Full Stack Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Wexler:

Wexler is building the best AI system for litigation on the planet. We work with some of the world’s largest law firms, helping them to solve their most complex cases, find the winning strategy in each matter, and create clarity from the chaos of documents and facts in each case. We are a rapidly growing, legal AI company based in London. Clifford Chance, HSFKramer, Goodwin, Addleshaw Goddard and more rely on us to help find the critical facts that can determine their chances of winning a case.

We’re backed with a $5.3M Seed by Pear VC, Seedcamp, The LegalTechFund + many leading industry angels.

We are building a comprehensive AI platform for managing, resolving and preventing legal disputes across Enterprise law firms and Fortune500 companies. We are growing 10x YoY and signing more eminent firms every month. Our system extracts, objective, cross referenced facts from millions of documents, helping litigators win more cases whilst saving months of working hours. In this way we ensure every client gets the representation they deserve.

AI is transforming the law, but most tools have focused on contract law or are generalist copilots that aggregate the tasks lawyers do across practices. Wexler is the leading gen-AI platform specifically built for the nuances of litigation, and our growth proves the story is resonating.

Full Stack Engineer:

We're seeking an entrepreneurial full-stack engineer who will work closely with the founders to architect, build and scale Wexler's agentic systems for document analysis, powered by our state-of-art fact extraction engine.

As a Software Engineer, you will work closely with the founding technical team and contribute to the technical architecture of our product and delivery of our ambitious product roadmap.

You'll play a key role in shaping the culture of our Technical organisation and will learn alongside expert Software and Machine Learning Engineers. You will rapidly take on more responsibility and have a clear path to a leadership position.

Please note we have two open positions for this role.

Responsibilities:

  • Architect, build and scale full-stack applications that power Wexler's agentic systems for document analysis

  • Develop customer-facing features, internal tooling and DevOps infrastructure to support our growing platform

  • Collaborate with AI engineers to integrate LLM capabilities into production-ready software systems

  • Build robust, scalable backend systems using modern technologies and cloud infrastructure

  • Create intuitive user interfaces that allow legal professionals to interact seamlessly with AI-powered tools

  • Contribute to technical architecture decisions and help establish engineering best practices

  • Work directly with customers to understand their needs and rapidly iterate on solutions

Technical Must-Haves:

  • Strong experience with Node.js and TypeScript for backend development

  • Strong Python experience for AI system development

  • Proficiency with PostgreSQL for database design and optimisation

  • Hands-on experience with AWS cloud services and infrastructure

  • Full-stack development experience with modern frontend frameworks

  • Experience building scalable, production-grade systems

  • Understanding of DevOps practices and CI/CD pipelines

You will be:

  • A builder with a track record of shipping new product features or architectures in a fast-paced environment

  • Driven by building fantastic product experiences - you can put yourself in the users shoes and understand their struggles

  • Fascinated by AI and excited to build products at the bleeding edge of this once in a lifetime platform shift (but you don't need to have any prior AI experience)

  • Full-stack and happy to get stuck in where needed most, be it working on customer-facing features, internal tooling or improving our DevOps

  • Excited to work in a startup environment. You're excited by the idea of speaking with customers in the morning and shipping features to solve their problems in the afternoon. You're ok with priorities changing and you're comfortable with risk

  • Someone who values working with people who are low ego, ambitious and pragmatic

  • Comfortable figuring out how to build things you haven't built before

  • Excited to work in-person from our office in London. We work from the WeWork in Aldwych, and we spend 4 days a week in person

What We Offer:

  • Competitive salary and significant equity

  • Huge autonomy and ownership. You will be designing and building the core systems that power AI for some of the most expert users in AI

  • Budget for learning and professional growth

  • Bi-annual team retreats

  • Work closely with experienced founders and a team of AI scientists and engineers

About the opportunity:

Legal AI has caught the attention of VCs and the wider tech world, but the reality is adoption with users is low in the enterprise, with roughly 20% of lawyers using AI tech. Of those lawyers, most are transactional or contract lawyers and they use generalist platforms that look to aggregate the tasks lawyers do but do not go deep into specific workflows. That's where Wexler is different. We are a 'scalpel' rather than a 'Swiss Army knife', meaning we go deep into the workflows that can decide how a legal case is won. We have extremely positive feedback from lawyers, and we have an ambitious roadmap of features to expand our coverage while retaining the forensic detail that makes our product great.

Some topics you'll think about:

  • Delightful ‘agentic’ product experiences: Legal AI has largely revolved around AI assistants. we are building workflows that solve specific tasks for expert users. You will be obsessed with defining and building these features.

  • Scale: architecting systems that scale with our commercial growth, delivering each user a delightful, performant and magical experience.

  • Security: our customers treat their clients with the highest degree of sensitivity and security. The software we build meets the highest standards of security, ever evolving in the world of AI.

Note: If you think you don't quite fit the bill but you'd still be interested in chatting for a different role, get in touch.

jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Software Engineering Intern

We’re seeking an exceptional engineering intern to join Wexler and work directly alongside our expert Software and Machine Learning Engineers. This is a hands on roll, you will contribute to the agent infrastructure of our product, push the product forward through blue sky projects, and have direct impact on a product that expert lawyers use every day.

We are ideally seeking 2026 graduates (or strong second-year students) from top UK universities in Computer Science or a closely related discipline. If you are obsessed with building things, intellectually curious, and excited by the frontier of applied AI, we’d love to meet you.

About Wexler

Legal AI has caught the attention of VCs and the wider tech world, but the reality is adoption with users is low in the enterprise, with roughly 20% of lawyers using AI tech. Of those lawyers, most are transactional or contract lawyers and they use generalist platforms that look to aggregate the tasks lawyers do but do not go deep into specific workflows. That’s where Wexler is different. We are a ‘scalpel’ rather than a ‘Swiss Army knife’, meaning we go deep into the workflows that can decide how a legal case is won. We have had extremely positive feedback from lawyers, and we have an ambitious roadmap of features to expand our coverage while retaining the forensic detail that makes our product great.

Responsibilities:

  • Build and develop our agentic infrastructure

  • Partner with the technical team to ideate, develop, and execute innovative, forward-looking (“blue sky”) initiatives that enhance and evolve the Wexler product.

  • Contribute to customer-facing interfaces that allow legal professionals to interact seamlessly with the product

  • Work alongside AI engineers to integrate LLM capabilities into production systems

  • Participate in technical architecture discussions and learn engineering best practices from a strong founding team

  • Think about the problems that matter most: delightful agentic experiences, performance at scale, and enterprise-grade security

Technical skills:

  • Back-end: Proficiency in Node.js / TypeScript or Python — ideally both. Comfort writing clean, testable server-side code.

  • Databases: Familiarity with relational databases (PostgreSQL preferred). Understanding of schema design and querying.

  • Front-end: Exposure to a modern JS framework (React is our stack). Able to translate product ideas into clean UI.

  • Cloud & DevOps: Any experience with AWS, CI/CD pipelines or containerisation is a bonus — not a requirement.

  • AI / ML: No prior AI experience is required. Curiosity about LLMs and how they work is all we ask.

  • A 2026 graduate (or strong 2nd-year) from a top UK university, studying Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a closely related field

  • A builder — you have personal projects, hackathon experience, or open-source work that demonstrates you love creating things

  • Intellectually curious and excited by the once-in-a-generation platform shift happening in AI

  • Full-stack and comfortable getting stuck in wherever needed, be it a customer-facing feature, an internal tool or a performance fix

  • Energised by a startup environment: priorities move fast, customers are close, and your work ships the same week it’s written

  • Someone who values working with people who are low ego, ambitious and pragmatic

  • Comfortable figuring out how to build things you haven’t built before, and asking smart questions when you need to

  • Based in (or willing to relocate to) London for the internship. We work 4 days a week in person from our WeWork in Aldwych

What We Offer:

  • Real ownership: You will be designing and building the core systems that power AI for some of the most expert users in AI

  • Mentorship from experienced software and machine learning engineers, including direct access to the founders

  • A clear path to a full-time Software Engineer role for outstanding interns

jobs.title: Investor - Pear
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Pear

Pear VC is a venture capital firm that partners with founders from day zero, often before an idea, product, or team exists. We are former founders and operators who get in the trenches with founders, providing the hands-on mentorship, recruiting support, and operational insights needed to turn a raw idea into a category-defining company. We focus on supporting founders to nail the fundamentals of product-market fit long before the rest of the world takes notice. Our early bets on visionary builders have grown into industry leaders like DoorDash, Gusto, and Guardant Health.

We’re looking for an Investor to connect with world-class builders, help us find the next generation of iconic founders, and welcome them into the Pear community. This role is focused on finding extraordinary builders at the earliest possible point of their founding journey and connecting them to the Pear ecosystem for investment.

The Role:

This is a high-agency role focused on one singular mission: finding the best future founders before anyone else does. You will be the face of Pear in different communities, tasked with mapping the future founder ecosystems and building deep, authentic relationships with the next generation of founders.

While this role will focus mainly on sourcing and community building, you will be mentored and trained by one of the Investment Partners at Pear. This role will participate in weekly Deal Flow conversations and allow someone access to some of the leading early stage investors in the world.

Responsibilities:

  • Build authentic relationships with current founders, engineers, researchers, professors, and recent grads with the goal of finding the who are the best future founders.

  • You should be attending, hosting, and organizing events that will steer these builders to participate in either our PearX program and lead to seed dealflow

  • You will act as the connective tissue between these builders and Pear, making sure we’re the first call when someone is thinking about starting a company.

  • You will be able to select, leverage and manage a group of student Fellows who can assist you in being the eyes and ears of campus while also organizing and running any programs to attract the top builders

  • There is no perfect way to do this job so you will have to find creative ways to connect, and get access to these people

Qualifications:

  • Deep passion for Sourcing: You have a good taste of what exceptional people are like and you genuinely love the "hunt" for talent

  • Proprietary Network & Respect: You are a figure that the founder network will have great respect for. You speak their language, understand their world, and have the credibility to be their first call when they start something new.

  • High Autonomy & Trusted Judgment: We trust you to work autonomously. This includes having full confidence in your independent judgment to identify "who" is a great founder and the agency to move deals forward without hand-holding.

  • Builder at heart: You have experience building things as a previous founder, early at a startup, or an organizer of some group. You’re exceedingly resourceful, and consistently find ways to do more with less.

  • Relationship builder: You’re approachable, optimistic, authentic, and easy to connect with.

  • Reliable and hyper organized: No matter how busy life gets, you don’t drop balls or leave people hanging.

  • Curious by nature: You operate from first principles, dive deep into how things work, and are constantly exploring new ideas, products, and markets with open eyes.

  • You do whatever it takes: You’re a high-agency problem solver. You break through walls to get stuff done and step up without hesitation.

  • Passionate to be great: You want to be known in the industry as someone who can find the most elite humans and be known as the one who found the next category defining company

Nice-to-haves:

  • B.S. in Computer Science or equivalent.

  • 5+ years of professional experience in the startup/tech world

  • Former venture backed founder

  • Active involvement in on-campus startup communities.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Senior Product Manager

About Us

Our mission: Eradicate health disparities by empowering the teams who care for underserved families.

BridgeHealthAI partners with Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) and community organizations to ensure every patient gets the care and benefits they deserve without drowning care teams in paperwork.

Our platform automates high-friction tasks like outreach, insurance verification, eligibility checks, follow-ups, referrals, and scheduling. With modern AI and automation, we help teams close care gaps faster, protect revenue, reduce administrative burden, and stay focused on patients.

Born out of Harvard and MIT and backed by Pear VC, Flare Capital, and Glen Tullman (founder of Livongo), BridgeHealthAI is a fast-growing, seed-stage company trusted by leading community health centers. We are purpose-built for the safety net, helping clinics scale access, reduce burnout, and deliver equitable care for the 30M+ patients served by FQHCs each year.

The Role

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager with 5+ years of product management experience and meaningful experience in healthcare or health tech to help us turn complex healthcare operations into simple, scalable products.

This is a highly hands-on, customer-facing product role. You'll work directly with health center executives, frontline teams, engineers, operations, and the founders to deeply understand problems, identify what we should build, and drive products from discovery through launch and iteration.

You'll be in the room with our customers. You'll lead working sessions, understand how their workflows operate today, identify where things break down, and work alongside them to design better ways of working. You'll turn those conversations into product ideas and clear product direction, bring concepts back to customers for feedback, and partner closely with engineering to bring the best solutions to life.

Our customers operate in complex environments where workflows often span patients, staff, payers, EHRs, external systems, phone calls, spreadsheets, and manual follow-up. Your job is to make that complexity feel simple.

You won't manage a backlog from a distance. You'll talk to users, map workflows, make product decisions, write clear requirements, test ideas, and stay close to customers after launch to make sure what we build actually works.

You'll have significant ownership over our product as we scale from high-value workflows into a broader platform for healthcare administrative automation.

What You'll Do

  • Own products and workflows end-to-end, from customer discovery and problem definition through development, launch, measurement, and iteration.

  • Lead product conversations directly with customers, including healthcare executives, operational leaders, and frontline staff.

  • Co-design solutions with customers. Understand how work happens today, identify where it can improve, and translate real operational problems into better workflows and product experiences.

  • Facilitate ambiguous customer conversations and create clarity. Ask the right questions, surface the real problem, align on the desired future state, and determine what the product team should do next.

  • Turn customer conversations into scalable product direction, separating individual feature requests from broader problems and identifying patterns across customers.

  • Prototype and test ideas quickly. Put concepts in front of users, gather feedback, and iterate before and after launch.

  • Translate complex healthcare operations into intuitive products that reduce administrative burden and make it easier for teams to get work done.

  • Partner closely with engineering to translate customer and business needs into clear product requirements and make thoughtful tradeoffs around scope, usability, speed, and reliability.

  • Map current-state and future-state workflows, including the people, systems, decisions, handoffs, and exceptions involved.

  • Define and track success metrics and use product data, operational outcomes, and customer feedback to understand what's working and where we should improve.

  • Prioritize thoughtfully, balancing customer needs, product strategy, engineering capacity, scalability, and business impact.

  • Stay close to implementation and adoption. The job doesn't stop when something ships; you'll work with customers and internal teams to understand how products perform in the real world and continuously improve them.

  • Help shape the broader product strategy and roadmap as BridgeHealthAI grows.

Qualifications & Requirements

Required

  • 5+ years of product management experience, with meaningful experience building products in healthcare or health tech.

  • Experience owning meaningful products or workflows from discovery through launch and iteration, rather than primarily managing requirements or a backlog.

  • Strong understanding of healthcare operations and the complexity of building products involving patients, providers, payers, clinical teams, and administrative staff.

  • Exceptional customer-facing skills. You're comfortable leading working sessions with healthcare executives and frontline teams, asking the right questions, challenging assumptions respectfully, and turning messy conversations into clear product ideas and decisions.

  • Demonstrated ability to conduct strong customer and user discovery, identify the underlying problem behind a request, and translate insights into scalable solutions.

  • Strong product and user experience judgment. You care about making complex workflows feel simple and intuitive and can recognize when a product experience is confusing, overly complicated, or solving the wrong problem.

  • Strong business judgment. You understand how product decisions connect to customer value, adoption, scalability, and company priorities—not just feature delivery.

  • Experience working closely with engineers and translating ambiguous customer and business problems into clear product direction and requirements.

  • Comfortable working with modern AI tools. You regularly use tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Claude Code, or similar tools to work faster across research, synthesis, prototyping, and product development. You don't need to be an engineer, but you should be curious about what's possible with AI and comfortable experimenting with new tools.

  • Strong analytical skills and comfort using both quantitative and qualitative information to evaluate product performance and make decisions.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication. You can communicate clearly with engineers, healthcare executives, frontline staff, customers, and founders.

  • Ability to operate effectively in ambiguity. You can create structure where none exists, make decisions with incomplete information, and move quickly without waiting for a perfect playbook.

  • Strong ownership mindset. You care about whether something actually works for the customer—not simply whether the feature shipped.

Strongly Preferred

  • Experience at an early-stage health tech startup, ideally Seed through Series B.

  • Experience building technology for providers, health systems, FQHCs, Medicaid populations, payers, or value-based care organizations.

  • Experience with healthcare administrative workflows such as eligibility, enrollment, revenue cycle, patient access, care coordination, referrals, scheduling, prior authorization, or patient engagement.

  • Familiarity with EHRs, payer systems, and healthcare data workflows.

  • Understanding of HIPAA, PHI, healthcare compliance, and the reliability expectations associated with healthcare software.

  • Experience building products that combine technology with real-world operational workflows, rather than purely self-service software.

  • Experience designing products for users who are busy, operationally constrained, and not necessarily highly technical.

  • Comfortable using modern tools to quickly prototype or communicate product ideas.

  • Chicago-based or willing to work hybrid. We value regular in-person collaboration, particularly for product and strategy work.

What We Value

  • Customer Obsession: You want to understand how the work actually happens. You get close to users, ask questions, observe workflows, and care about solving the real problem—not simply delivering the requested feature.

  • Product Judgment: You can simplify complexity and make thoughtful tradeoffs between customer needs, usability, scalability, speed, and business impact.

  • Business Judgment: You understand that not every customer request should become a feature and can connect product decisions to the broader company strategy.

  • AI-Native Mindset: You're comfortable using emerging AI tools to research, synthesize, prototype, and work more effectively. You treat AI as a tool to move faster—not a substitute for judgment.

  • Bias Toward Action: You don't need months of research before testing an idea. You find the fastest responsible way to learn, get feedback, and iterate.

  • Clarity: You can walk into an ambiguous customer conversation and leave with a clear understanding of the problem, the desired future state, and what should happen next.

  • Ownership: You see things through. Shipping is a milestone, not the finish line.

  • Systems Thinking: You understand that healthcare workflows rarely exist in isolation and think through downstream effects, handoffs, edge cases, and operational realities.

  • Learning Agility: You can quickly learn a new healthcare workflow, customer environment, technology, or AI tool and apply that knowledge effectively.

  • High Standards: Healthcare users need products they can trust. You care deeply about quality, usability, reliability, and the details that determine whether a workflow succeeds.

Why Join Us?

  • Build with Purpose: Your work will directly support organizations serving underserved communities, helping keep patients covered while reducing the administrative burden on care teams.

  • Build Directly With Customers: You'll have unusually close access to healthcare leaders and frontline teams and work alongside them to turn real problems into products.

  • Own Meaningful Product Problems: You'll tackle complex, high-value healthcare workflows where great product thinking can eliminate hours of manual work.

  • Shape the Product: We're early enough that you'll have significant influence over what we build, how we build it, and how our product organization develops.

  • Use AI Where It Matters: Help us apply AI and automation to real healthcare problems where the impact can be measured in better patient access, less administrative work, and stronger operations.

  • Small Team, Big Ownership: You'll work closely with founders, engineers, customers, and operations, with significant autonomy and responsibility from day one.

  • Real Traction, Early-Stage Opportunity: Join a seed-stage company with paying customers and clear market demand while there's still significant opportunity to shape the foundation.

How to Apply

Apply via the link, and also send your resume and a brief note explaining why BridgeHealthAI and why this problem space directly to hello@bridgehealthequity.com.

Our interview process will focus on how you think about customers, healthcare workflows, product judgment, prioritization, and turning ambiguous problems into products that work in the real world. We move quickly and respect your time.

BridgeHealthAI is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of race, gender, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability status, or other protected characteristics.

jobs.title: Field & Demand Generation Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Field & Demand Generation Manager — Bevado

Location: New York City · Full-time · In person

Salary: $70,000–$90,000 annual base salary, plus equity and benefits

Reports to: Head of Growth
Travel: Typically one to two trips per month

Bevado builds AI workers that help retailers and property managers manage customer operations across calls, texts, email, and chat. We’re hiring a Field & Demand Generation Manager to turn events, relationships, and campaigns into a repeatable source of qualified pipeline.

This is an early-career opportunity with meaningful ownership. You’ll work directly with our Head of Growth to run our events program, support demand generation campaigns, and measure what’s driving revenue. You should be equally comfortable hosting a room of prospective customers and digging into a spreadsheet to understand whether an event paid off.

What you’ll own

  • Events from start to finish. Plan and execute conferences, dinners, and hosted events, including audience selection, invitations, vendors, budgets, logistics, and follow-up.

  • A monthly pipeline goal. Work with the Head of Growth to set targets tied to event investment, then own execution against those targets.

  • Performance and spend tracking. Track event-sourced and event-influenced pipeline, conversion rates, cost per opportunity, and revenue. Partner with Growth to understand customer lifetime value relative to acquisition cost (LTV:CAC), and use those insights to decide where to invest.

  • Reliable sales handoffs. Make sure every event lead is captured in the CRM, assigned to an owner, and followed up with promptly. Keep context and next steps clear so no opportunity falls through the cracks.

  • Customer and prospect experiences. Organize dinners and events that strengthen existing client relationships, create new opportunities, and help move active deals forward.

  • Webinars and outbound campaigns. Help produce and host webinars, manage promotion and follow-up, and execute selected cold email campaigns.

  • Sales gifting. Coordinate thoughtful gifting that helps the sales team build relationships and advance opportunities.

  • AI-powered workflows. Use AI and automation to improve research, outreach, event operations, reporting, and follow-up. Build repeatable processes that let the program scale.

What we’re looking for

  • Approximately 0–2 years of experience. Candidates with backgrounds in marketing, psychology, sales, banking, consulting, or analytics are encouraged to apply. We welcome recent graduates, and relevant internships, projects, and experience organizing events count.

  • Exceptional people skills and emotional intelligence. You build rapport quickly, listen well, and make customers, prospects, and teammates feel taken care of.

  • Strong analytical instincts. You’re comfortable working with spreadsheets, interpreting campaign results, and connecting spend to business outcomes.

  • Excellent organization and follow-through. You can manage multiple moving pieces, anticipate problems, and close the loop without repeated reminders.

  • Strong communication. You write clearly, speak confidently, and feel comfortable hosting conversations and representing Bevado at events.

  • Practical proficiency with AI tools. You can translate a business goal into a clear strategy and workflow, use AI to execute more effectively, and evaluate the quality of its output. Experience building automations or connecting tools is a plus.

  • Initiative and curiosity. You take responsibility for results, learn quickly, and bring ideas for making the next campaign better.

Experience with CRM systems, event planning, webinars, or cold email tools is helpful. Prior ownership of a full demand generation program isn’t required.

Travel expectations

This is a high-travel role, typically requiring one to two trips per month to attend events, meet clients and prospects, and host dinners. Travel is a core part of the position, so please make sure you’re comfortable with that commitment before applying.

How you’ll grow

You’ll receive direct coaching from the Head of Growth while building your own operating playbook. As you demonstrate results, you’ll have the opportunity to own a larger events budget, expand into additional demand generation channels, and help build the team around the program.

The long-term path is toward leading Bevado’s events function and growing into a Director of Demand Generation role as the business scales.

Compensation and benefits

  • $70,000–$90,000 annual base salary.

  • Meaningful equity.

  • Competitive benefits.

  • Unlimited PTO.

  • Company-paid lunch and dinner in the office.

  • Direct mentorship from the Head of Growth.

  • Opportunity to take on greater responsibility and leadership as you grow.

jobs.title: Founding AI Engineer - Manhattan Labs
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the team

We’re building the AI-native compliance platform for community banks and financial institutions.

Regulatory pressure is intensifying. Financial crime is becoming more sophisticated. Compliance teams are overwhelmed by manual workflows and fragmented systems. Community banks, despite managing billions in assets, lack the tooling to keep up.

We’re building the intelligence layer that changes that: a system that can answer questions like
“What is our exposure to this entity across all customers?”
- with a defensible, auditable answer.

Our team includes engineers and researchers from Stanford, Carnegie Mellon, and IIT Madras, and we’re backed by Tier 1 investors and experienced operators who understand the massive opportunity in modernizing financial crime compliance with AI.

Learn more at https://manhattanlabs.co/

.

Description of the role

This is a true founding engineer role. You won’t just ship features - you’ll define the system.

You’ll architect and build an AI-native platform that operates as the investigative brain for compliance teams. This includes agentic reasoning systems, large-scale document ingestion, and user-facing tools that must stand up to regulatory scrutiny.

You will take the product from early-stage MVP to a secure, reliable, enterprise-grade system used by financial institutions.

By reimagining KYB and AML as autonomous intelligence, you'll help build the platform that becomes the default compliance infrastructure for thousands of community banks, that each manage assets worth billions of dollars. You'll work directly with the founding team, own technical decisions, and lay the foundation for a potentially massive and fast-growing SaaS company.

Responsibilities and potential impact

  • Design, build, and operate RAG and agentic systems over complex financial data (corporate registries, sanctions lists, beneficial ownership, adverse media), with clear evaluation metrics for accuracy, latency, and cost

  • Develop scalable backend services for document processing (PDF/OCR/CSV), async job queues, case lifecycle orchestration, and risk scoring with confidence-driven UX and human-in-the-loop controls

  • Own the productionization of AI systems, including evaluation pipelines, dataset/version management, and safe rollout strategies (A/B testing, guardrails, fallback behavior)

  • Harden the platform for enterprise: auth controls, role-based access, audit trails, backups, and monitoring with measurable SLOs

  • Establish CI/CD, deployment pipelines, runbooks, and incident response practices from the ground up

  • Propose and engage in cutting-edge AI research related to our mission, particularly around agentic reasoning over regulatory and financial data

  • Work directly with the founding team to define architecture, technical roadmap, and product direction

Must haves

  • 1+ years of experience on technical projects with startup experience strongly preferred

  • Strong TypeScript and Python skills across modern frontend and backend stacks

  • Hands-on experience shipping LLM integrations or RAG systems into production user-facing products

  • Experience with document processing, entity extraction, and structured data extraction from messy real-world sources

  • Solid grasp of API design, relational databases, and async job processing systems

  • Proven track record taking a product from "works locally" to reliable production at growing scale

  • Debugging instincts across frontend, backend, infra, and data boundaries - and an ownership mindset to match

Nice to haves

  • Knowledge of KYC/KYB/AML workflows, sanctions screening, beneficial ownership data, or regulated fintech

  • Experience with LangChain, LlamaIndex, or similar AI orchestration frameworks

  • Familiarity with banking APIs, core banking systems, or financial data providers

  • Familiarity with OCR and document intelligence pipelines

  • Background in fintech, compliance, RegTech, or other regulated industries

  • Cloud deployment experience and DevOps knowledge in security-sensitive environments

  • Strong product intuition and user experience focus

What we offer

We believe in generous, top-tier compensation and benefits for our employees:

  • Competitive salary and equity

  • 100% health, dental, and vision coverage

  • Commuter stipend

  • Regular team events and off-sites

jobs.title: Founding Sales Development Representative
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Location: New York City, in person 5 days a week
Experience: 9 to 15 months of BDR experience, ideally selling into SMBs
Compensation: Competitive base plus commission

About Frontdesk

Frontdesk builds AI workers for customer-facing businesses. We help SMBs and mid-market companies answer calls, qualify leads, follow up with customers, manage tickets, and automate customer operations across voice, SMS, chat, email, and CRM.

We are growing quickly and looking for a hungry Cold BDR who can help us build a repeatable outbound engine.

The Role

You will be responsible for identifying, researching, and booking meetings with qualified prospects. This is a high-volume outbound role for someone who already has some BDR experience and wants to level up quickly in a fast-moving startup.

You should be comfortable cold emailing, calling, testing messaging, handling rejection, and working closely with sales leadership to figure out what works.

What You’ll Do

  • Prospect into SMB and lower mid-market accounts across target verticals

  • Build lead lists using tools like Apollo, LinkedIn, and company websites

  • Write and send personalized cold emails

  • Make daily cold calls to decision-makers

  • Book qualified meetings for Account Executives or founders

  • Track activity, responses, and learnings in the CRM

  • Test messaging across different industries and buyer personas

  • Learn the product deeply enough to explain the value clearly

  • Give feedback on what prospects are saying in the market

What We’re Looking For

  • 9+ months of BDR, SDR, or outbound sales experience

  • Experience selling to SMBs is strongly preferred

  • Strong written communication skills

  • Comfortable making cold calls every day

  • High ownership, high energy, and strong follow-through

  • Competitive and resilient, without needing a lot of hand-holding

  • Curious about AI, startups, and sales

  • Organized enough to manage a high-volume outbound process

  • Excited to work in person with a fast-growing team

Nice to Have

  • Experience selling SaaS, AI, telecom, CRM, customer support, or SMB software

  • Experience using Apollo, HubSpot, Salesforce, Instantly, Smartlead, Clay, or similar tools

  • Prior success booking meetings through cold email and cold calling

  • Experience prospecting into industries like property management, healthcare-adjacent businesses, home services, retail, or local services

What Success Looks Like

In your first 30 days, you will learn the product, understand our target customers, shadow sales calls, and start booking meetings.

By 60 days, you will be running your own outbound sequences, calling prospects daily, and consistently generating qualified meetings.

By 90 days, you will be one of the core drivers of our outbound pipeline and helping us identify which verticals, messages, and campaigns are working best.

Why Join

  • In person in NYC (5 days a week) office required

  • Join an early-stage startup growing quickly

  • Work directly with founders and senior sales leaders

  • Sell a product that is easy for SMBs to understand and care about

  • Learn how to build outbound from the ground up

  • Strong path to Account Executive for top performers

  • Excited to work in person with a fast-growing team

jobs.title: Lead Account Strategy Partner (Forward-Deployed, Healthcare Data)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Flyway Health

At Flyway Health, we start from a simple conviction: somewhere in every life sciences team's data is a finding that would change their next quarter, and we've built the system to go find it. Our autonomous agents run across a variety of healthcare data, surfacing the signals commercial teams don't have time to look for – shifting prescriber dynamics, gross-to-net drift, unescalated lookalike patients, payer coverage changes, and more, all discovered autonomously.

We've supported four launches in our first six months and are growing rapidly. We've raised roughly $4M to date and are backed by Pear VC, Greg Field, and a group of industry-veteran advisors — and we're here to change how commercial life sciences operates.

 

The Role

As Lead Account Strategy Partner (ASP), you own client delivery as our most senior ASP — running your own portfolio of accounts and setting the standard the rest of the team works to.

ASPs are the bridge between a client's commercial life sciences questions and the answers our system can produce. You do this work directly by wielding the system with skill, steering it, interfacing with our engineering team to integrate new datasets, and applying the judgment that turns raw healthcare data into insight a brand or market access team can act on. As the senior voice on a small, growing team, you set the bar for how delivery is done and help the ASPs around you do their best work — with the runway to grow into leading the function as we scale.

This is a hands-on, technical role. You'll be in the weeds: setting up and working through claims and other healthcare datasets, learning about new therapeutic areas, running analyses through our system, and interrogating what comes back. You'll need real comfort with the fundamentals of data science paired with the client instinct to turn a result into something a commercial team can act on.

What You'll Do

  • Own end-to-end delivery for your accounts: scope the client's question, run the analysis through our system, and deliver insights commercial life sciences stakeholders can act on.

  • Operate our proprietary agentic system day to day — directing it, integrating new datasets, and pressure-testing its output. The system is built; the skill is using it well and knowing which parts of the output are most pertinent to the client.

  • Work primarily with healthcare claims data, and quickly build intuition for the other datasets we use — picking up an unfamiliar dataset and understanding its shape and limits fast.

  • Read, follow, and reason critically about SQL and the results it returns.

  • Spot and account for the nuances of real-world healthcare data: sparsity, coverage gaps, claims lag, capture rates. Distinguish a genuine signal from a data artifact.

  • Translate fluidly between client commercial strategy and the technical realities of the data and the system.

  • As our most senior ASP, set the bar for how delivery is done and help the ASPs around you sharpen their craft — with the runway to grow into leading the function as the team scales.

  • Work directly with the founders and influence future product roadmap.

What We're Looking For

Required

  • Commercial life sciences fluency from day one — you understand how pharma/biotech commercial teams operate (market access, brand strategy, commercial analytics, patient journey, HCP targeting, etc.).

  • LLM-native: genuinely comfortable working with AI and agentic tools — prompting, steering, and evaluating model output is second nature.

  • A data science or data engineering background (either in training / in practice)

  • A sharp, analytical mind that interrogates data and outputs rather than taking them at face value.

  • Comfort with healthcare claims data, or the demonstrated ability to ramp on a new dataset very quickly.

  • Comfort in a client-facing role, with strong people skills.

  • 2+ years of relevant industry experience.

Nice to Have

  • Prior client-facing, consulting, or forward-deployed experience.

  • Familiarity with additional healthcare dataset types (EHR/EMR, lab, specialty pharmacy, etc.).

  • Light scripting (e.g., Python).

  • 5+ years of experience.

What We Offer

  • $150-180k base salary + stock options

  • Eligibility for medical, dental, and vision insurance, with employee premiums fully covered by Flyway

  • Hybrid NJ/NYC with flexibility for remote candidates

jobs.title: Part-Time Video & Social Producer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Endless Commerce

Endless Commerce is a SaaS company building the operational backbone for consumer brands growing from Shopify into retail and beyond. Think about the brands you actually buy: apparel, beauty, food, home goods. We’re the software that keeps their inventory, orders, and supply chain from imploding as they scale.

Our podcast is called Commerce is Chaos.

About Samantha

Samantha Rose is CEO, co-founder, serial founder, and the host of Commerce is Chaos. She’s built brands from her kitchen table to national retail and has been sharing what she’s learned (unfiltered) on LinkedIn, Substack, and the podcast for years. She has a real audience, a distinct voice, and a lot happening in front of and behind the camera we’d like you to capture.

The Role

We’re looking for a part-time Content Creation Associate to join us in San Clemente weekly. This is a hands-on, real-work role, rather than a “watch and learn” internship. You’ll be doing the actual shooting and editing that feeds Samantha’s presence across LinkedIn, Instagram, and TikTok. This role reports to the Head of Content.

What you’ll do:

  • Edit short-form clips from Commerce is Chaos podcast episodes for LinkedIn and social: punchy, well-paced, no fluff

  • Shoot IRL footage and B-roll of Samantha at and around the office for use across platforms

  • Help build out a library of vertical video content optimized for TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and LinkedIn video

  • Support our small but mighty content team in executing a weekly social cadence

Who We’re Looking For

You’re studying film, communications, marketing, media, or something adjacent — or you’ve just been editing on your own long enough that your skills are solid and ready to roll. You know your way around editing tools, have opinions about pacing, are deadline-oriented, and can adhere to a content calendar.

jobs.title: Founding GTM Operator
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Job

Founding go-to-market role at a fast growing, venture-backed B2B AI startup. Own our growth engine end-to-end.

Position: Founding GTM Operator (Full-Time)

Reporting to: CEO

Location: San Francisco (4 days/week in person)

Compensation: $90,000-$110,000 base salary, plus your choice of equity or a bonus linked to company revenue (bonus expected to be $10,000+ for this role).

Company Overview

Lenders spend over $24B every year hiring agents to perform manual, repetitive servicing work. Existing AI solutions try to automate this, but they treat regulatory guardrails as an afterthought - meaning they can’t guarantee compliance and can’t be trusted with critical servicing workflows.

Kato takes a different approach.

Regulations aren’t an afterthought - they’re the foundation. We start with a regulatory rules system and layer an AI decision engine on top. With this architecture, we’re building an AI-powered servicing platform that automates critical workflows across every channel with full compliance and best-in-class recoveries.

We are starting today with a compliance first Voice AI agent that handles outbound and inbound loan servicing calls. We have grown ARR 6x this year and are already in production with major names in the fintech lending space like Bilt Rewards, Bluevine and Parafin.

Kato is founded by a team with deep operating expertise in financial services and software engineering:

  • Pratik Risbud (CEO/Co-Founder): Former Investment Banker at Goldman Sachs and led Credit/Operations at Brex

  • David Zhu (CTO/Co-Founder): Former Software Engineer at Google and Engineering Manager at Brex

Kato is backed by institutional capital from Pear VC and angel investors from top tech companies such as Brex, Bridge, and Square.

The Role

We already know how to find and close customers. We are now hiring our Founding GTM Operator: a generalist who owns demand generation and turns our go-to-market into a repeatable growth engine. This is one of the most critical hires at Kato and you'll work directly with the CEO.

On the outbound and conference side, that means getting sharper and more sophisticated about how we find customers - tracking the right buying signals, testing new plays, and expanding our conference presence.

And on the brand side, it’s wide open. We want to turn Kato into a household name in the lending space. You'll own building our presence from scratch: events, webinars, LinkedIn posts, newsletters, blogs. When someone in this industry thinks about AI for servicing & collections, we want them to think of Kato first.

Across both, we don't just want someone who can run the motion - we want someone who builds the system behind it, using AI and automation to take out as much manual work as possible.

This role is a fit if you have 1-3 years of experience and:

  • You are a former founder, or owned GTM / growth at an early-stage startup

  • You have done either sales development (SDR/BDR) or demand-focused marketing (MDR, field or event marketing) - a role where you were measured on pipeline/revenue.

This role is not a fit if:

  • If your background is analytics / data focused without direct exposure to revenue

  • If your background is pure brand or content marketing measured on reach and impressions

Key responsibilities

Outbound & Lead Generation (50%)

  • Build and maintain a comprehensive database of the lending market

  • Own end-to-end outbound: research, list building, copy, multi-channel outreach (email + LinkedIn), message refining

  • Create and manage nurture campaigns for older or dormant leads

  • Run Kato’s conference efforts (e.g. outreach, marketing campaigns, booths)

  • Systematize relentlessly - automate list building, signal tracking, personalization, and sequencing wherever you can with AI and other tooling

Content & Marketing (30%)

  • Define Kato’s content strategy by creating blog posts, newsletters, and other top-of-funnel materials

  • Launch Kato’s marketing efforts - e.g. webinars, in person events

  • Systematize relentlessly - automate research and content drafting wherever you can with AI and other tooling

Sales Operations (20%)

  • Build custom collateral for prospect meetings and keep Kato's core materials current

  • Own GTM reporting - define what we measure (e.g. outbound conversion rates, pipeline velocity, meeting-to-opportunity conversion) and act on them

Requirements

We covered who this role is a fit for above. Beyond that you:

  • Have 1-3 years of full-time work experience and a Bachelor’s degree in Business or related field

  • Are a structured thinker who questions assumptions and reasons independently, rather than taking things at face value

  • Are coachable and quick to act on feedback

  • Have exceptional written communication

  • Are comfortable operating with high agency and driving independent progress toward company goals

  • Have strong attention to detail, organization, and follow-through

  • Are AI-native and automation-minded, with a track record of using AI tools to remove manual work

  • Are proficient with common business tools such as Google Workspace (e.g. Google Docs, Google Sheets) and Slack. Experience with CRM systems like Hubspot preferred

Why Join Us

  • Work with founders that have built and scaled financial products for 9+ years

  • Own real scope from day one - you'll own core parts of our revenue engine and see your work hit customers fast.

  • Work hard on things that matter. This won't be a 9-to-5, but we don't believe in busy work. We work hard on the problems that actually move the business and don't waste your time on the ones that don't.

  • Get unmatched career acceleration: you’ll learn sales, GTM strategy, and startup execution at a depth few roles offer.

jobs.title: Founding Sales Lead
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About TeachShare

TeachShare is on a mission to simplify the daily instructional process so teachers can focus on the moments that matter. To do this, we are building a self-improving, easily digestible, daily plan for teachers that is grounded in their student's concept mastery, along with their institution's framework and curriculum.

We are the only Plan, Teach, Assess platform for K-12.

TeachShare is used by teachers across 60,000 schools. We got here with a full-time team that is entirely engineers. For two years we've been heads-down on product depth, and the bet is paying off: we're growing fast month over month, and our last two months have been our best ever.

The role

Every deal so far has been closed by the founders. We have real inbound from schools & districts of teachers that use and love us. What we don't have is anyone whose whole job is turning that demand into a real pipeline.

That's you. You're our first sales leader and our first go-to-market hire. This is a founding role. You'll take what's worked from founder-led sales and build the entire sales function from scratch: process, tooling, messaging, all of it.

What you'll do

  • Own the full sales cycle with schools and districts, from first conversation to signed contract

  • Run the motion that's already working and make it repeatable without you or us in every call

  • Build the systems that don't exist yet: CRM hygiene, outreach, qualification, pricing conversations, contracting

  • Get fluent in how districts actually buy: budget cycles, purchase orders, RFQs, vendor registration, committees, pilots, and partnerships

  • Feed what you hear in the field directly into positioning and roadmap, working side by side with the founders

  • Lay the groundwork for the team that comes after you: the playbook, the onboarding, the first hires

What we're looking for

  • 3+ years in a quota-carrying sales role, with B2B or B2G sales cycle experience (EdTech a plus, not required)

  • Self-directed. You're comfortable operating without an existing playbook, because there isn't one yet

  • Genuinely interested in education and making educators' lives easier, not just selling into it

  • Resilient with setbacks. You treat a pitch that doesn't land as data and iterate quickly

  • Operator mindset. You're as comfortable designing a process as running one

  • Optimistic & a someone who hustles.

Why TeachShare

Work with the founding team and have real influence and ownership over product and go-to-market. A product teachers already pull into their schools for you. And the chance to build a sales org's foundation from the ground up instead of inheriting someone else's.

The work matters, too. We're fostering classroom cohesion for hundreds of thousands of teachers and hundreds of schools and districts. You'd be the person who brings it to thousands more.

We are backed by the best investors in education - Reach Capital, with support from Pear VC.

Compensation: $90-200k + OTE & meaningful ownership. Range depends on experience and location.

jobs.title: Head of Content
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Head of Content

Bevado is hiring a Head of Content with a strong focus on video content creation.

Location: New York City, NY (onsite, five days a week).

This is a full-time, onsite role in New York City for someone who can turn software, product ideas and customer problems into videos people want to watch. You'll report directly to our Head of Growth and work closely with our founders to plan content, make it, publish it and improve it.

We care more about aptitude, creative judgment and the quality of your work than years on a resume. We’re looking for someone with 2–5 years of relevant experience.

What you'll do

  • Own video production from idea to finished asset, including research, concepts, hooks, scripts, filming, editing, captions and publishing.

  • Create short-form videos and ad creative for Meta and Instagram, plus short-form and long-form YouTube content.

  • Help build our founders' presence on LinkedIn through video and written content that sounds like them and gives their audience something useful.

  • Make product demos, launch videos and software explainers that communicate clear value to both SMB and enterprise buyers.

  • Plan the content calendar with our Head of Growth, test original formats and improve creative using audience feedback and performance data.

  • Contribute to product marketing and special projects, including landing page copy and design, lifecycle campaigns and broader brand initiatives. Use AI tools to speed up research, production and iteration.

What we're looking for

  • A strong video portfolio. You can make polished, engaging content and explain the creative choices behind it.

  • You find yourself making videos, editing and experimenting with content in your own time. Personal accounts, side projects, internships and work for other companies all count.

  • Good instincts for hooks, storytelling, pacing, sound, captions and visual presentation. You know how to make a video clear and hold someone's attention.

  • The ability to take an idea and turn it into a finished video with ownership, initiative and consistent execution.

  • Clear written and spoken English, curiosity about software and AI, and an interest in understanding the product and the people who use it.

  • Comfort working closely with a small team, taking feedback and trying new approaches.

A strong bonus

You've helped build an audience through content you produced for a personal brand, another company, an internship or a side project. Show us examples of work that earned attention, engagement or audience growth, and explain what you personally created. There is no minimum follower count.

Show us your work

Send ben@bevado.com an email with any work that shows your content creation skills, whether that's a video, a social media profile, a portfolio link, or results from content you've created.

Include your strongest examples and a short explanation of what you personally handled, such as the concept, script, filming or editing.

Benefits

Annual base salary: $75,000–$130,000 USD.

  • Free lunches five days a week

  • Unlimited paid time off (PTO)

  • Equity

  • Health insurance

jobs.title: Founding Pharmacist-in-Charge & Head of Compounding - Turnkey Robotics
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Description

We're building the modern compounding pharmacy of the future by pairing the best pharmacy experts with modern technology. We aim to offer the most reliable, fast turnaround, and highest quality compounding services to providers and telehealth partners. We're backed by the investors that backed Palantir, SpaceX, and Neuralink.

 

Role Description

We are seeking our Founding Pharmacist-in-Charge (PIC) and Head of Compounding for a full-time, on-site role based in the San Francisco Bay Area. The individual will lead and oversee all nonsterile and sterile compounding pharmacy operations, ensuring compliance with regulatory standards and developing efficient workflows. The individual will serve as the first pharmacist in charge for the facility and will be responsible for building a top tier pharmacist and pharmacy technician team. Key responsibilities will include production of sterile and nonsterile compounds and building out our compounding facility, building out our quality and compliance processes, managing pharmacy staff, optimizing inventory, and contributing to strategic planning efforts to strengthen the organization's pharmacy infrastructure. The candidate will play a key role in creating and implementing processes that ensure safety, efficiency, and innovation within the pharmacy practice.

 

Ideal Qualifications

  • Strong expertise in Pharmacy, Pharmacy Practice, and in particular in hands-on compounding of both sterile and non-sterile compounds

  • 5+ years of work experience at a 503A compounding facility, ideally as the pharmacist in charge

  • Strong experience and familiarity with USP 795 / 797 compliance

  • Active pharmacist license including a California License

  • Experience with compounding pharmacy software

  • Demonstrated leadership capabilities, with experience managing and mentoring a team

  • Knowledge of regulations and compliance standards related to sterile and nonsterile compounding

  • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to implement new processes effectively

  • Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) degree or equivalent qualification is preferred

  • Entrepreneurial instincts and a desire to bring modern software and robotic automation into the compounding world to produce prescriptions of the highest quality and safety

 

Compensation

  • 150-275k depending on experience, alongside competitive cash bonuses and 90th percentile equity compensation.

jobs.title: MassHealth Enrollment Specialist & AI Operations
jobs.descriptionHtml:
MassHealth Enrollment Specialist & AI Operations

Help patients keep their health coverage — and help us build a better way to do it.

BridgeHealthAI is building technology for the healthcare safety net.

We work with community health centers to make sure patients don’t lose access to healthcare because of paperwork, missed deadlines, or an impossible-to-navigate system. Our platform helps health centers identify patients who need support, reach them at scale, and automate the administrative work that takes their teams hours today.

We’re a small, fast-moving team building at the intersection of healthcare, AI, and health equity. BridgeHealthAI was born out of Harvard and MIT and is backed by Pear VC, Flare Capital, and Glen Tullman, founder of Livongo.

Now, we’re looking for someone who really knows MassHealth.

The Role

Our technology can identify a patient who is at risk of losing coverage, reach them, and figure out where they’re getting stuck.

You’ll help take them the rest of the way.

That might mean getting on the phone with a patient to complete their renewal, figuring out what a confusing MassHealth notice actually means, tracking down a missing document, calling MassHealth with them, or making sure an application actually made it across the finish line.

But this isn’t just an enrollment processing role.

You’ll also be the MassHealth expert inside our company. You’ll work directly with our product and operations teams to show us where patients get stuck, what our technology gets wrong, and what we could automate or redesign to make the process dramatically easier.

We’re still early, which means there’s a lot to figure out. If you like the idea of doing great work with patients and helping build a better system from the ground up, you’ll probably enjoy this role.

What You’ll Actually Do

jobs.title: Founding Growth & Strategy Lead - Optexity (USA)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Optexity

Optexity is a product-driven research lab building clinical reasoning and computer use models on data no other lab can reach. We deploy directly inside clinics and hospitals — including systems with no APIs, using integration infrastructure we've built and open-sourced — and in return become their preferred partner. That gives us proprietary clinical reasoning trajectories from practicing physicians, and a feedback loop between real patient encounters, our models, and the products built on top of them.

We're a small, fast-moving founding team with multiple published papers in NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR etc and background from Apple, Amazon, Microsoft, CMU, IIT.

We are backed by world-class investors and leaders like Jeff Dean, Neotribe VC, PearVC, Together Fund and Zapier Fund.

How we work

  • Customer obsession — we start with the customer and work backwards

  • Intellectual honesty — ideas matter more than titles; we communicate directly and assume good intent, even in disagreement

  • Bias for action — we build and learn with customers rather than debate in the abstract

  • Extreme ownership — we own outcomes, not just tasks, and see problems through

About the role

This is not an EA role, and not a narrow sales or marketing role — it's a hands-on operator role for someone who can take an ambiguous business problem, structure it, and drive it to a result, working directly with the founders.

Why this role exists

Partnerships, developer community, recruiting, and market research all sit on the founders' plates today, alongside product and engineering. We need someone to own that surface area — not run a fixed playbook, but build one as they go.

What you'll do

  • Build relationships with private equity firms active in healthcare — especially those owning multi-location clinics or hospital groups — as a channel into the market

  • Develop long-term relationships with hospitals and clinics; understand their workflows and pain points before and during deployment

  • Build a developer-adoption strategy: engage directly with developers building in health AI, learn what they need, and turn that into adoption

  • Source, screen, and run early conversations with candidates for open roles

  • Run market research to find new avenues for growth and partnership

  • Represent Optexity at industry events, conferences, and developer communities — and convert conversations into pipeline

  • Own ambiguous, cross-functional projects that need speed, judgment, and persistence — whatever matters most that week

What we look for

  • Comfortable with a wide-open mandate — this role looks different in month six than on day one

  • Strong communication and relationship-building, with real follow-through

  • Excellent research, synthesis, and structured thinking

  • Operates in ambiguity without waiting for perfect instructions

  • Willing to do unglamorous, high-value work

  • Genuine interest in healthcare workflows, and the ability to learn the space fast

Nice to have

  • Venture capital or business/strategy team experience

  • Prior healthcare exposure

  • Existing relationships with developers in health AI

  • Experience in fast-moving startups

What you get

  • Direct, daily work with the founders, plus exposure to board and investor conversations

  • True zero-to-one scope — company-building, not function-executing

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, AI Agents
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Socratix AI

 

Socratix AI builds AI coworkers for fraud, financial crime, and compliance teams. Our agents investigate every transaction and user around the clock — gathering evidence across core banking activity, check images, device intelligence, and screening hits so every case opens with the full picture, not a dozen tabs.

 

As one of our first engineers, you'll shape the technical foundation of Socratix AI (YC S25). We build AI agents that investigate fraud and financial crime for banks, credit unions, and leading fintechs — agents that reason through real cases, gather evidence across systems, and produce decisions that stand up to regulators.

 

You'll design and ship production AI agents that fraud and compliance teams rely on every day, collaborate directly with founders on product strategy, and partner with both large enterprises and cutting-edge fintechs.

 

This is a high-impact role with massive scope for growth — you won't just be building features, you'll be defining how agentic AI transforms financial crime operations.

 

Our Culture: F.O.R.C.E.

We believe the right culture builds unstoppable teams. At Socratix, our values spell F.O.R.C.E. — the driving force behind everything we do:

  • First Principles – We start from truth, not tradition, and solve problems in original ways.

  • Ownership – What you work on is yours to elevate; we take accountability and act with confidence.

  • Relentlessness – We finish what we start, turning obstacles into breakthroughs.

  • Customer First – Every decision is measured by one standard: does this make our customers’ lives easier?

  • Empathy – We respect differing perspectives, design for human needs, and build trust that lasts.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Build agents end to end: LLM orchestration, tool use across a growing set of MCP integrations, retrieval, and multi-agent workflows that automate real investigations.

  • Own the layer that makes agents trustworthy — eval harnesses, guardrails, audit trails, human-in-the-loop review. When your agent decides, a bank acts on it.

  • Ship fast and close to users: code in prod your first week, direct customer contact, your work catching actual fraud. Design and deliver production-grade AI agents.

  • Experiment relentlessly. New models, new techniques, new tooling — you'll have license to try everything and keep what wins.

  • Turn frontier into product. You'll spend real time probing what the newest models can do, then ship the parts that survive contact with real fraud cases

  • Shape roadmap and strategy with the founders. Small team, zero bureaucracy, maximum ownership.

 

What We’re Looking For

  • A systems thinker. You reason about the whole machine — data flow, failure modes, latency, cost, what breaks at 10x — not just the function you're writing. Agents are distributed systems with a nondeterministic component in the middle; if that framing excites you, keep reading.

  • You've shipped real things with LLMs — production systems, prototypes with users, obsessive side projects.

  • Deep engineering fundamentals. Frameworks are details you pick up in a weekend (we're mostly Python on AWS). What matters is that you can design, ship, debug, and operate a production system end to end.

  • 0 → 1 builder. Ambiguity and speed energize you instead of stressing you out.

  • Roughly 2–4 years of engineering experience — or a portfolio that makes that line irrelevant.

  • Prior experience in startups is a plus

  • Curiosity about fintech, fraud, or building AI where the stakes are real and regulated.

 

Benefits

We believe in generous, top-tier compensation and benefits:

  • Competitive salary and equity benchmarked to top tech companies.

  • Paid meals during workdays.

  • 100% health, dental, and vision coverage.

  • Hybrid schedule - in-office 3 days a week.

  • Commuter Benefits

  • Unlimited PTO.

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Forward Deployed Engineer

New York City · In Person · Travel Required

 

ABOUT FRONTDESK

Frontdesk is building AI workers that run customer operations across voice, text, email, and chat.

Over the last year, the size of the contracts we've been closing has increased roughly 10x, with several enterprise deals now reaching six figures and beyond.

At that scale, deployment stops being simple.

Our largest customers need custom integrations, complex workflows, outbound orchestration, legacy systems connected, and dozens of edge cases handled before AI can actually run meaningful parts of their business.

We're looking for the person who wants to own that problem.

 

THE ROLE

We're hiring our Forward Deployed Engineer.

You will take our hardest enterprise customers from:

"We want Frontdesk to do this" → "It's live in production."

There won't always be a playbook.

You might fly to a customer's office, sit with their operators, understand a workflow nobody has documented properly, design the solution, and then build the missing integration or product capability yourself.

You won't throw requirements over the wall to another team. You'll work directly in the codebase and own the outcome.

And once it works, you'll ask the most important question:

How do we make sure we never have to build this from scratch again?

You'll take what you learn in the field and turn it into reusable Frontdesk product, infrastructure, and deployment primitives.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own our largest and most technically difficult enterprise deployments.

  • Work directly with customers to understand how their businesses actually operate.

  • Build integrations, workflows, internal tooling, and product capabilities needed to get them live.

  • Travel onsite when being in the room helps us solve the problem faster.

  • Work across voice, SMS, email, chat, APIs, data, LLMs, and workflow orchestration.

  • Debug whatever is blocking a deployment, even when the problem sits outside Frontdesk.

  • Identify patterns across customers and turn one-off solutions into scalable product.

  • Work closely with the founders and engineering team on what Frontdesk should build next.

 

BUILD AND LEAD THE FUNCTION

We expect this to become a major function inside Frontdesk.

At first, you'll be extremely hands-on. You'll write code, work with customers, and personally own deployments.

As we scale, we expect you to build and eventually lead the Forward Deployed Engineering organization.

That means defining how we deploy enterprise AI, hiring the team, building the playbooks, and determining how Forward Deployed Engineering works with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Customer Success.

We're looking for someone who doesn't just want a job.

We're looking for someone who wants to build something from zero, own a massive surface area, and eventually lead the organization they create.

 

YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF YOU

  • Are a strong software engineer who wants more ownership than a traditional engineering role provides.

  • Love talking to customers and solving real problems, not just working from tickets.

  • Are comfortable jumping across the stack and learning whatever is necessary.

  • Have strong product intuition and naturally think about how to generalize what you build.

  • Thrive when the problem is ambiguous and there is no existing playbook.

  • Move extremely quickly and take personal ownership over outcomes.

  • Would rather own an entire problem than a small piece of a large system.

  • Could see yourself starting a company someday, or already think like a founder.
