jobs.title: Chief of Staff - Blueberry
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the role

Blueberry is building the autonomous 1:1 marketer. Our AI enables brands to drive personalized conversations with every customer, supercharge lifecycle marketing outcomes, and drive revenue.

We’re:

  • Enterprise-proven: Trusted by the San Francisco 49ers, Paris Hilton’s portfolio, and DTC brands generating $100M+ in annual sales.

  • Growing quickly: In six months, continuously doubled revenue and customers onboarded.

  • Talent-Dense: 8 people, 75% ex-founders

  • Early: The operating systems, playbooks, and leadership team that scale Blueberry are still being built.

AI is changing how every consumer brand communicates with its customers. We are defining that shift—and we’re looking for someone who wants their fingerprints on the company and category we build.

As Chief of Staff, you’ll work directly with Nima Mozhgani, our co-founder and CEO, and operate across Blueberry’s most important initiatives.

This role is for an exceptional operator who wants to become a founder, COO, or define their career with operational excellence.

What you’ll do

  • Multiply the CEO: Take critical projects from ambiguous idea to finished outcome across GTM, fundraising, hiring, and expansion.

  • Drive customer success: Own the operating cadence across enterprise customers and move them from pilot to deep activation and expansion.

  • Build the operating system: Create the processes, automations, tools, and company rhythms that let Blueberry scale without losing speed.

  • Orchestrate execution: Keep the entire company aligned on owners, priorities, deadlines, and outcomes.

  • Incubate new initiatives: Take on high-priority problems until they are solved, systematized, or ready for a permanent owner.

  • Shape company communication: Prepare board materials, investor updates, decision memos, and company-wide narratives.

  • Finish: Close loops relentlessly. We believe the last 10% is 100% of the challenge.

What we’re looking for

  • 3-7 years in a high-performance environment: Consulting, banking, venture, startup ops, or a company you built yourself.

  • You get things done: You have a proven track record of building things, launching game-changing projects, and having impact on tight timelines.

  • You bring order to chaos: You turn vague, messy problems into clear plans and measurable outcomes.

jobs.title: Account Executive (SMB)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Account Executive (SMB)

New York City · Full-time · In person

Compensation

$150,000–$225,000 annual on-target earnings (base salary + commission), plus meaningful equity.

 

About Frontdesk

Frontdesk is building AI workers that run customer operations across voice, text, email, and chat. We are starting with the property management industry.

Our AI handles real work across the customer journey, from answering inbound calls to following up with leads, coordinating workflows, and taking action across the systems businesses already use.

We're growing quickly and moving upmarket. Over the last year, the size of the contracts we've been closing has grown roughly 10x, with several opportunities now reaching six figures and beyond. You're joining at an ideal stage: we've established repeatability and early playbooks, but they're still young enough for you to meaningfully shape how we scale them.

 

About the Role

We're hiring our second Account Executive to help build the next stage of our sales organization.

This is a true full-cycle role. You'll own prospecting, cold outreach, discovery, demos, follow-up, negotiation, and close.

You'll initially focus on SMB customers, with most deals around $8K–$25K ACV. If you're consistently performing, you'll have the opportunity to move quickly into larger mid-market and enterprise accounts.

There are no territories. If you find a great account, go win it.

You'll have support from SDRs, marketing, founders, and the broader team, but you'll own your pipeline and your number.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Own your pipeline from first touch through signed contract.

  • Prospect aggressively through cold calls, email, referrals, events, and creative outbound.

  • Run discovery, product demonstrations, negotiations, and closing.

  • Sell directly to owners, operators, and executive stakeholders.

  • Multi-thread accounts and keep deals moving.

  • Consistently meet and exceed sales targets.

  • Bring customer feedback directly into Product and Engineering.

  • Help shape our messaging, sales process, hiring bar, and team culture.

  • Attend industry events and meet customers in person when it helps win.

     

Why Great Salespeople Should Join Frontdesk

  • You're joining as AE #2. You'll have a real influence on how the sales organization gets built.

  • No territories. Great accounts are there for you to go after.

  • Real ownership. We care about the outcome, not whether you followed a prescribed process.

  • Increasing deal sizes. Start by mastering $8K–$25K deals, then earn your way into increasingly large accounts.

  • Build the playbook. A lot of what our future sales team does will come from what you figure out now.

  • Sell something customers actually care about. AI is fundamentally changing how businesses handle customer operations, and we're still early in that transition.

 

Requirements

  • At least 3 years of professional sales experience, including a quota-carrying B2B software Account Executive role and a track record of meeting or exceeding quota.

  • Comfortable generating your own pipeline rather than relying entirely on inbound or SDRs.

  • Strong cold calling, discovery, demo, negotiation, and closing skills.

  • Competitive and highly accountable for your number.

  • Excellent follow-up and pipeline management.

  • Comfortable selling to both operators and executives.

  • Able to learn a technical product quickly.

  • Excited by an early-stage environment where the playbook is still being written.

  • Based in New York City and able to work in person from our NYC office.

Preferred: experience selling to property managers, multifamily operators, or real estate businesses; previous BDR/SDR experience; and experience at an early-stage or similarly sized technology company.

 

Why Join

You're joining early enough to actually shape the company.

This isn't a role where you'll inherit a territory, run someone else's playbook, and optimize around the edges. You'll help us figure out how Frontdesk sells, who we hire, how we compete, and what kind of sales culture we build.

If you're great, the scope will expand quickly.

Come help us build the sales organization you would have wanted to join.

jobs.title: Founding GTM - Blueberry
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the role

Blueberry is building the autonomous 1:1 marketer. Our AI enables brands to drive personalized conversations with every customer, supercharge lifecycle marketing outcomes, and drive revenue.

We’re:

  • Enterprise-proven: Trusted by the San Francisco 49ers, Paris Hilton’s portfolio, and DTC brands generating $100M+ in annual sales—all through founder-led sales.

  • Growing quickly: Over the past six months, we’ve repeatedly doubled both revenue and customers onboarded.

  • Talent-dense: Eight people, 75% ex-founders.

  • Early: The GTM playbooks don’t yet exist at Blueberry.

AI is changing how every consumer brand communicates with its customers. We are defining that shift—and we’re looking for someone who wants their fingerprints on the company and category we build.

This is not a traditional AE role. You’ll own our DTC motion end-to-end, partner with our Founder & CEO on enterprise sales, and grow into building and leading Blueberry’s GTM engine.

This role is for someone who can sell today and wants to become a GTM leader—or eventually build a company of their own.

What you’ll do

  • Own revenue: Create pipeline and close DTC business end-to-end (discovery, demos, follow-ups, negotiation, and closing) while partnering with our Founder & CEO on enterprise opportunities.

  • Create demand: Use outbound, events, partnerships, referrals, and creative prospecting to reach buyers wherever they gather.

  • Build the GTM engine: Determine which customers, messages, channels, and sales motions convert, then build the systems and playbook that scale.

  • Use the team: Partner with our Founder & CEO, GTM Engineer, and Storyteller to build target lists, campaigns, collateral, and systems that increase your output.

  • Do whatever it takes: Move mountains to help Blueberry 10x revenue in six months.

What we’re looking for

  • 2-5 years in sales or customer-facing GTM: You have personally generated pipeline and closed business.

  • DTC fluency: Experience selling to or working inside consumer brands, e-commerce, or the surrounding ecosystem is strongly preferred.

  • You’re a hunter: You create opportunities without depending on inbound demand, brand recognition, or perfect collateral—and deliver results on tight timelines.

  • You learn quickly: You test new messages and channels, study what works, and improve through repetition.

  • You’re a top 1% communicator: You write sharp outreach, run compelling demos, and earn trust with founders and marketing executives. People understand you and like you.

  • You’re low ego: You care about the customer, the number, and the company—not whose job something is.

Why this role?

You will build Blueberry’s revenue engine, not inherit someone else’s. But you’ll do so with a strong support system between the Founder & CEO, GTM Engineer, and Storyteller to help you execute.

You’ll own DTC from day one, work directly with our Founder & CEO on enterprise sales, influence the product, and develop the playbook and team that follow you.

Exceptional performance can create a path toward leading a significant part of Blueberry’s GTM organization.

jobs.title: Clinical Physician (Full-time or Part time)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Optexity

Optexity is a product-driven research lab building clinical reasoning and computer use models on data no other lab can reach. We deploy directly inside clinics and hospitals — including systems with no APIs, using integration infrastructure we've built and open-sourced — and in return become their preferred partner. That gives us proprietary clinical reasoning trajectories from practicing physicians, and a feedback loop between real patient encounters, our models, and the products built on top of them.

We're a small, fast-moving founding team with multiple published papers in NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR and backgrounds from Apple, Amazon, Microsoft, CMU, and IIT.

We are backed by world-class investors and leaders including Jeff Dean, Neotribe VC, PearVC, Together Fund, and Zapier Fund.

How we work

  • Customer obsession — we start with the customer and work backwards

  • Intellectual honesty — ideas matter more than titles; we communicate directly and assume good intent, even in disagreement

  • Bias for action — we build and learn with customers rather than debate in the abstract

  • Extreme ownership — we own outcomes, not just tasks, and see problems through

Why this role exists

We're building a clinical AI assistant that sits inside real practices — surfacing care gaps, assembling pre-visit prep, flagging risk, and suggesting treatment plans. None of that works without physicians defining what "correct" means.

Most clinical advisor roles are a monthly call where someone reacts to a demo. This one isn't. You'll be in the product loop weekly: deciding what the assistant should flag, what a good summary actually looks like at 7:50am before a 15-minute visit, and grading where the model is wrong and why. Your judgment becomes our ground truth and our evaluation standard.

We're looking for physicians across internal medicine, cardiology, oncology, and other specialties — both to go deep in your own domain and to help us understand where workflows diverge across specialties.

What you'll do

  • Define what the assistant should surface. Which care gaps matter, which risk signals are worth an interruption, and which are noise that erodes trust. Translate clinical shorthand into precise, checkable criteria.

  • Shape the pre-visit summary. What belongs in it, in what order, at what length — and what a physician actually reads versus scrolls past.

  • Specify clinical search. What you'd want to pull from the chart before a visit, how you'd phrase it, and what a complete answer looks like.

  • Judge the AI. Review model-generated risk flags, differentials, and treatment plans against your own reasoning. Score them, explain the gap, and tell us whether a miss is dangerous or merely different.

  • Build ground truth. Help us construct real-case evaluation sets and rubrics that reflect actual standard of care, not textbook answers.

  • Pressure-test the product. Sit in on design decisions and tell us when something wouldn't survive contact with a real clinic day.

  • Contribute to publications. We publish benchmarks and technical reports; clinical co-authorship is available and encouraged.

Ideal candidate

  • MD or DO, board-certified or board-eligible

  • Currently practicing or recently practicing — active clinical context matters more than titles

  • Internal medicine, cardiology, oncology, or an adjacent specialty; primary care and multi-specialty experience especially welcome

  • Day-to-day fluency in an EMR (Epic, eClinicalWorks, Athena, ModMed, or similar) and an honest view of where it fails you

  • Opinionated about clinical workflow, and able to explain why something is right — not just that it is

  • Comfortable with ambiguity, direct feedback, and being asked "how do you actually know that?"

  • Genuinely interested in AI in medicine, including its failure modes

Nice to have

  • Clinical informatics training or CMIO-adjacent experience

  • Experience with quality measures and value-based care programs (HEDIS, MIPS, CPT Category II, HCC coding)

  • Prior work advising or building health tech products

  • Research or publication background

  • Experience training residents or fellows — the skill of articulating clinical reasoning out loud transfers directly

Commitment

  • Part-time: 5–15 hours/week, flexible around clinical schedules. Async-friendly, with a recurring weekly working session.

  • Full-time: for physicians ready to step into a founding clinical role and own clinical direction end to end.

Remote is fine. Occasional in-person time in San Francisco or at partner clinic sites is a plus.

What you get

  • Direct, daily work with the founders — no layers between your input and what ships

  • Real influence over a product that practicing physicians will use, not a pilot that dies in committee

  • Competitive hourly rate for part-time engagements; competitive salary and meaningful equity for full-time

  • Co-authorship on benchmarks and technical reports

  • Visa sponsorship available for full-time roles

jobs.title: Founding GTM
jobs.descriptionHtml:
What we build

Last year, natural catastrophes caused over $140 billion in US losses.

ResiQuant exists to keep the built world insurable as catastrophe intensifies.

Two nearly identical buildings can have completely different fates in an earthquake, hurricane, or wildfire — and the expertise necessary to tell them apart isn't available when underwriters need it most. That's where ResiQuant comes in.

Think Harvey, but for property underwriting: our AI agents do what used to take underwriting teams days and weeks — read messy broker submissions, virtually inspect buildings, validate the structural data that drives the vast majority of catastrophe loss variation, and price risk against a carrier's own guidelines — in minutes.

Who we are

A team of scientists, ex-founders, AI and structural engineers, and product builders from Pear and YC companies. Backed by LDV Capital, Pear VC, Foothill Ventures, and strategics. We've designed buildings, contributed to national building codes, and built products people love.

Co-founders Omar Issa and Francisco Galvis are structural engineering PhDs out of Stanford's Blume Earthquake Engineering Center — the birthplace of modern catastrophe modeling.

  • Omar is a second-generation structural engineer who deployed on post-disaster response at Ridgecrest and served on NIST and USGS code committees; previously Arup and KATERRA.

  • Francisco is a third-generation engineer who survived the 1999 Armenia, Colombia earthquake, ran post-earthquake inspections in Turkey and after Hurricane Ian, and led San Francisco's non-ductile concrete ordinance work; previously Thornton Tomasetti.

The role

Every logo we have was closed by the two founders — mapping workflows with chief underwriting officers, shadowing underwriters through renewals, partnering with shops from startup MGAs to publicly traded carriers.

You own the revenue engine that surrounds our selling: the machine that finds the right accounts in a finite market, gets us in front of them, and moves them to signature. The deals run five to seven figures, on sales cycles of one to three months. We keep the demos and the close to start — you own everything around them, and that boundary moves as your deals do.

You own the process. You run the machinery of every deal; the work is three engines:

Demand — get us into rooms. Own the account map. Run deeply researched outbound. Operate our warm channel — advisors, investors, and industry relationships — as a system instead of a lucky accident. Run conferences end-to-end: selection, pre-event outreach, the booth, and the 48-hour follow-up machine. Keep a lightweight content heartbeat alive.

Deal velocity — get rooms to signatures. Run the pilots: environments coordinated, customer data chased, evaluation cadence kept on rails. Own the critical middle of enterprise selling — security questionnaires, procurement steps, vendor onboarding. Build the collateral that closes: proposals, decks, the one-pager a champion forwards to their CFO.

The operating system — make it compound. Build the systems underneath everything above with the stack we already run (Attio, Claude Code) — account research, signal capture, follow-up automation. Own the pipeline numbers: the weekly review, conversion and velocity, the GTM slide in the board deck. Run the feedback loop from the market into product: objections, feature asks with business context, competitor moves.

Who fits

We index on agency over tenure. Our best-fit candidates are ex-founders, former chiefs of staff, BizOps operators, and operators who happened to pick up an MBA — roughly one to four years of doing real things. A GTM title is nice to have, not required. Insurance experience isn't required either; sharp people learn this market fast.

What is required: judgment on top of AI, not just fluency in it. Writing that sounds like a human. The presence to hold a conversation with a chief underwriting officer at a conference reception. And a track record of owning an outcome — a number that was yours alone — because everything in this role comes back to that.

You're not a fit if: you are unexcited about in person work / 5-days in office, or your proudest GTM story is a sequence you optimized; "the AI/script/tool told me that" has ever been your answer to why; you measure your week in activity; you need the demo seat on day one; or you've never owned a number that was yours alone.

Why join us

  • Mission: Keep the built world insurable as catastrophe intensifies — this work decides whether coverage exists at all.

  • Founding seat: The first commercial hire. The playbook you write is the one every GTM hire after you runs.

  • Real ownership: The revenue engine is yours end to end — accounts, systems, conferences, collateral — working directly with both founders every day.

  • Growth: A front-row seat to enterprise AI sales, in the room from first touch to signature with some of the most sophisticated shops in the market.

What we offer

  • Competitive salary + founding-hire equity.

  • Full medical, dental, and vision benefits; 401(k) with company match.

  • Daily lunch + commute support in our SF office.

  • Relocation support for the right candidate.

Think Harvey, but for property underwriting: our AI agents do what used to take underwriting teams days and weeks — read messy broker submissions, virtually inspect buildings, validate the structural data that drives the vast majority of catastrophe loss variation, and price risk against a carrier's own guidelines — in minutes.




WHO WE ARE

A team of scientists, ex-founders, AI and structural engineers, and product builders from Pear and YC companies. Backed by LDV Capital, Pear VC, Foothill Ventures, and strategics. We've designed buildings, contributed to national building codes, and built products people love.

Co-founders Omar Issa and Francisco Galvis are structural engineering PhDs out of Stanford's Blume Earthquake Engineering Center — the birthplace of modern catastrophe modeling.

 - Omar is a second-generation structural engineer who deployed on post-disaster response at Ridgecrest and served on NIST and USGS code committees; previously Arup and KATERRA.

 - Francisco is a third-generation engineer who survived the 1999 Armenia, Colombia earthquake, ran post-earthquake inspections in Turkey and after Hurricane Ian, and led San Francisco's non-ductile concrete ordinance work; previously Thornton Tomasetti.




THE ROLE

Every logo we have was closed by the two founders — mapping workflows with chief underwriting officers, shadowing underwriters through renewals, partnering with shops from startup MGAs to publicly traded carriers. 

You own the revenue engine that surrounds our selling: the machine that finds the right accounts in a finite market, gets us in front of them, and moves them to signature. The deals run five to seven figures, on sales cycles of one to three months. We keep the demos and the close to start — you own everything around them, and that boundary moves as your deals do.



You own the process. You run the machinery of every deal; the work is three engines:



Demand — get us into rooms. Own the account map. Run deeply researched outbound. Operate our warm channel — advisors, investors, and industry relationships — as a system instead of a lucky accident. Run conferences end-to-end: selection, pre-event outreach, the booth, and the 48-hour follow-up machine. Keep a lightweight content heartbeat alive. 

Deal velocity — get rooms to signatures. Run the pilots: environments coordinated, customer data chased, evaluation cadence kept on rails. Own the critical middle of enterprise selling — security questionnaires, procurement steps, vendor onboarding. Build the collateral that closes: proposals, decks, the one-pager a champion forwards to their CFO.

The operating system — make it compound. Build the systems underneath everything above with the stack we already run (Attio, Claude Code) — account research, signal capture, follow-up automation. Own the pipeline numbers: the weekly review, conversion and velocity, the GTM slide in the board deck. Run the feedback loop from the market into product: objections, feature asks with business context, competitor moves.




WHO FITS

We index on agency over tenure. Our best-fit candidates are ex-founders, former chiefs of staff, BizOps operators, and operators who happened to pick up an MBA — roughly one to four years of doing real things. A GTM title is nice to have, not required. Insurance experience isn't required either; sharp people learn this market fast.

What is required: judgment on top of AI, not just fluency in it. Writing that sounds like a human. The presence to hold a conversation with a chief underwriting officer at a conference reception. And a track record of owning an outcome — a number that was yours alone — because everything in this role comes back to that.

You're not a fit if: you are unexcited about in person work / 5-days in office, or your proudest GTM story is a sequence you optimized; "the AI/script/tool told me that" has ever been your answer to why; you measure your week in activity; you need the demo seat on day one; or you've never owned a number that was yours alone.




WHY JOIN US

 - Mission: Keep the built world insurable as catastrophe intensifies — this work decides whether coverage exists at all.

 - Founding seat: The first commercial hire. The playbook you write is the one every GTM hire after you runs.

 - Real ownership: The revenue engine is yours end to end — accounts, systems, conferences, collateral — working directly with both founders every day.

 - Growth: A front-row seat to enterprise AI sales, in the room from first touch to signature with some of the most sophisticated shops in the market.
   


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive salary + founding-hire equity.

 - Full medical, dental, and vision benefits; 401(k) with company match.

 - Daily lunch + commute support in our SF office.

 - Relocation support for the right candidate.

jobs.title: AI Implementation Analyst (Construction Management) - Gryps
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We are a product-focused organization that dreams big and achieves those dreams. Our customers are large players in the construction industry. This is an opportunity to be part of a nimble team where every individual becomes an expert in their area. We work fast, iterate quickly, and create a product that transforms how our customers work through AI.

This is the place for you if you’ve worked in a role at the intersection of AI, automation, data analytics, construction tech, construction management, and innovative technology—and you’re looking for the next leap in your career.

We’re a growing company backed by Primary Ventures, LDV Capital, Pear VC, and other top investors. You will work directly with the CEO and our customers—large organizations that own and operate hospitals, universities, and public infrastructure. You’ll have the opportunity to shape our data strategy by exploring various data sources and datasets, running exploratory AI models, and providing analytics that support customer decisions. This is a unique chance to join early and shape your career with Gryps.

Must Haves

  • Have an undergraduate or Master’s degree in a quantitative field (e.g., mathematics, engineering, statistics, or similar) or construction management

  • 2+ years of work experience involving quantitative data analysis and complex problem-solving in construction

  • Proficiency in SQL and Python, along with experience using Quicksight, Power BI, Tableau, Jupyter Notebook, or other data visualization and exploration tools

  • Have 2+ years of construction industry experience

  • Possess excellent interpersonal and communication skills

  • Are curious, a great listener, and enjoy working with customers to find data-driven ways to support decision-making

You would love your job if you:

  • Are customer-obsessed and love helping people apply AI in their workflows

  • Are looking to join a small team and grow with it

  • Get excited by creating new processes, working with data, and innovating data applications

  • Are intrigued by how AI and RPA will change the construction industry

  • Love collaborating across teams to solve problems

  • Want to grow your career in customer success, data analytics, data science, or machine learning

  • Are passionate about disrupting the construction industry with technology

  • Are a fast learner or have a deep understanding of technology systems in the construction industry

  • Love working with data to uncover patterns and insights

What you'll be doing:

  • Understanding customer decision-making and identifying data that can influence those decisions

  • Analyzing data structures from construction systems or public data sources

  • Setting up customer dashboards, reconfiguring business processes, or leading whiteboard sessions to map out customer data use

  • Identifying and proposing potential data sources that could support customer decision-making

  • Consulting with customers on how to leverage their data via the Gryps platform

  • Documenting data workflows, data policies, structures, standards, and procedures for customer systems

  • Developing and running advanced descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics using Jupyter Notebook and Python

  • Gathering feedback on current Gryps use cases and identifying new opportunities

We recognize you as an early joiner by:

  • Competitive compensation

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Medical, dental, and vision benefits

  • Flexible career path

  • Direct influence on our product and company roadmap

About the Company

Gryps is a NYC-based, VC-backed startup on a mission to revolutionize the $10T construction industry by transforming the way capital projects are managed by owners and operators of construction programs.

Our Robotic Process Automation and AI platform sets Gryps apart by automatically ingesting, understanding, augmenting construction data and automating workflows—delivering actionable insights and more efficient workflows through intelligent applications. Our products have already transformed operations for top owners and developers in the US by streamlining construction processes.

At Gryps, we foster a culture of innovation, where brilliant minds collaborate to solve complex challenges. Our diverse team of talented engineers and industry experts drives our continuous pursuit of excellence.

With an ambitious product roadmap and fresh funding to fuel our growth, Gryps is poised to transform the construction industry. To achieve this vision, we are seeking exceptional professionals to join our dynamic team and help bring our revolutionary ideas to life.

Join Gryps today and be a part of reshaping a $10T industry!

jobs.title: Customer Support Engineer (UK) — Phaselaw
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Location: United Kingdom

Type: Full-time

Salary: £35,000-£45,000

About Phaselaw

Phaselaw is the leading eDiscovery platform for in-house legal and privacy teams. We save teams thousands of hours with tools for document production and redaction. We're a Seed stage startup but are already working with some of the largest companies in the world and are more than doubling the business every quarter.

The Role

We’re looking for a Customer Support Engineer to help us support our growing customer base in the UK and Europe. You’ll report directly to our CTO and work closely with our entire team to ensure our customers are getting the most out of our products. This is a high-ownership, high-impact, high-growth role where you’ll directly shape the future of the business and will have the opportunity to build out how we support our customers going forward. You'll touch every part of the customer lifecycle and have opportunities to grow in both customer-facing and technical directions.

What You’ll Do

  • Be the first line of defense for customer tickets and questions

  • Build scalable, AI-enabled systems for customer support

  • Channel customer feedback to our product development team

  • Create educational resources for our customers

  • Assist with bug fixing and QA

What We’re Looking For

  • Proven interest in learning and teaching: You'll be educating customers every day and learning about our product and technical systems.

  • A passion for software products and an interest in diving into the technical weeds on them.

  • Excellent written and spoken communication skills to enable you to communicate well with customers.

  • Ability to juggle multiple priorities across competing customer requests

  • Interested in the sort of rapid growth that only early stage startups can provide.

  • Extreme ownership and attention to detail. You’re a person who never drops balls.

  • Coding knowledge and interest in growing your coding skills.

  • A bias for action: You ship fast and iterate based on feedback.

  • (Optional) Knowledge of the Privacy or Legal fields.

Why Join Us?

  • Impact: Your work will directly shape the future of the company.

  • Growth: High ownership, deep collaboration with company leadership and customers. Potential to grow into new roles and scopes as the company grows.

  • Speed: We move fast, ship often, and value autonomy.

  • Culture: Our team is kind, collaborative, inquisitive, and inclusive – and we want to keep it that way. We have high standards for quality and ethics, and help each other learn in order to reach our objectives. We think technology is best built by teams with a diversity of background, thought, and experience.

👒 Every team member is a human first, and we strive to create a culture and environment that supports your career goals and respects all of the hats you wear in life, not just the ones that earn you a paycheck.

Our Team

We were founded in 2023 by SaaS and data experts. Josh (CEO) led Chartbeat as CTO to $70M+ ARR and exit. David (CTO) led product at Cortico (MIT spinoff) from 0-> 1.

jobs.title: Head of AI Deployment
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Gryps

Gryps is an AI operating system for the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry. Institutional owners such as hospital systems, universities, and airport authorities run multi-billion-dollar capital programs on data scattered across emails, spreadsheets, network drives, and disconnected systems of record. Gryps connects that information and gives owner teams an AI operating system for their capital programs, so they can find answers, manage risk, automate their work and make decisions faster.

We are a product-focused organization that dreams big and achieves those dreams. Our customers are large players in the construction industry. This is an opportunity to be part of a nimble team where every individual is an expert in their area. We work fast, iterate quickly, and create a product that transforms how our customers work through AI.

This is the place for you if you’ve worked in a role at the intersection of AI, automation, data analytics, construction tech, construction management, and innovative technology—and you’re looking for the next leap in your career. You will have direct influence over the growth of Gryps within customer organizations, our product roadmap, and impact on the Gryps bottom line.

We’re a growing company backed by Primary Ventures, LDV Capital, Pear VC, and other top investors. You will work directly with the CEO and our customers—large organizations that own and operate hospitals, universities, and public infrastructure.

The Role

We're hiring a Head of AI Deployment to lead a team of 4–6 in turning Gryps deployments into measurable value for our customers. You'll own the full post-sale relationship: understanding each customer's program, designing the data strategy behind their deployment, identifying the use cases that matter most, guiding the implementation team to fast, repeatable time to value, and measuring the success of the deployment.

This is a player-coach role. You'll work directly with owner executives and program leaders while developing early-career professionals into strong implementers and advisors. You'll also be accountable for renewals and expansion, because customers who get real value are the ones who grow with us.

What You'll Do

Lead and develop the team

  • Manage, coach, and grow a team of 4–6 customer success and implementation professionals, many early in their careers. Set clear expectations, give direct feedback, and build their construction domain knowledge and client-facing confidence.

  • Build the playbooks, standards, and rituals that make delivery consistent: onboarding frameworks, implementation checklists, account reviews, and health scoring.

Define value and data strategy

  • Work with customers to find the highest-value use cases across their capital programs, such as cost and change tracking, schedule risk, document and contract intelligence, closeout, and portfolio reporting. Prioritize them by business impact and feasibility.

  • Design the data strategy for each use case: which sources to connect, how unstructured and structured data is organized and validated, and how outputs tie back to the customer's systems of record and decisions.

  • Turn customer outcomes into clear, quantified value stories that executives and champions can carry into their own organizations.

Own customer relationships

  • Serve as trusted advisor and executive sponsor for your accounts, from project and program managers up to VPs of Facilities, Capital Planning, and Real Estate.

  • Lead executive business reviews that connect product usage to program outcomes and set the agenda for what comes next.

  • Represent the customer's voice internally, partnering with Product and Engineering on requirements, feedback, and roadmap priorities.

Drive product engagement and implementation efficiency

  • Own adoption and engagement metrics across your book of business. Spot drifting accounts early and step in before they become risks.

  • Run implementation for speed and repeatability. Remove bottlenecks, standardize what can be standardized, and keep shortening time to first value and time to full deployment.

Own renewals and expansion

  • Own gross and net revenue retention for your accounts, including renewal forecasting, negotiation, and execution.

  • Find and close expansion opportunities such as new use cases, departments, programs, or campuses, working with Sales on commercial strategy and contracting.

What You Bring

  • 8+ years of construction domain experience, with a deep understanding of how capital projects are planned, delivered, and closed out, and the data that flows through each phase.

  • An engineering or quantitative background, such as a degree in civil, mechanical, or construction engineering, construction management, or another analytical field, plus comfort reasoning about data structures, metrics, and systems.

  • Executive presence. You're credible with senior owner leadership, can run a boardroom conversation, and can hold a point of view under pressure.

  • A track record of coaching early-career professionals and building teams that measurably improve under your leadership.

  • Clear, structured communication, written and verbal. You explain complex technical and data concepts simply to field teams and executives alike.

  • Experience designing data strategies, or a proven ability to connect business problems to data sources, workflows, and outcomes.

  • Commercial ownership. You're comfortable being accountable for renewal and expansion revenue.

Nice to Have

  • Experience at an owner organization, such as a health system, university, airport, public agency, or large real estate owner, managing capital programs from the owner's side.

  • Experience implementing or managing construction technology platforms such as Procore, e-Builder, Unifier, Kahua, or enterprise data and AI tools.

  • Familiarity with BIM, digital twins, GIS or facilities and asset management data.

  • Experience at an early-stage or high-growth software company.

How Success Looks in Your First Year

  • Customers reach first measurable value on a predictable, shortened timeline.

  • Every account has a documented use-case roadmap and data strategy tied to executive-level outcomes.

  • Your team runs on shared playbooks, and each team member has grown noticeably in skill and independence.

  • Strong gross retention and meaningful net expansion across your book of business.

jobs.title: Founding Deployment Strategist - Polynomic
jobs.descriptionHtml:
The current ad market sucks. At Polynomic, we’re reimagining performance marketing from the ground up. We believe that ads, in various new forms, will continue to be the primary business model of the internet and the backbone of growth in commerce. Yet performance marketing today is heavily dependent on outdated playbooks, guesswork, manual effort. jobs.title: Senior Scientist & Program Lead
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Senior Scientist & Program Lead | Enzymology

What We’re Building

Velocity Bio is a venture-backed startup spun out of Stanford University combining cutting-edge microfluidics with AI to accelerate discovery of next-generation therapeutics. We are building the world’s largest dataset of high-fidelity enzyme function to train AI models for allosteric drug discovery and accurate enzyme function prediction.

Recently, Velocity partnered with the Institute for Protein Design at the University of Washington, Argonne National Laboratory, and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory on a Department of Energy Genesis Mission project to harness AI for breakthrough enzyme design. With our partners, we’re building the missing, massive quantitative datasets of activity and structure for computationally-designed enzymes needed to unlock next-generation AI models to design enzymes de novo with unprecedented fidelity.

Your Impact

In this role, you’ll work closely with the founding team on our mission to unlock AI models for allosteric drug discovery and accurate enzyme function prediction. To do this, you’ll scale large-scale, high-fidelity enzyme function datasets, develop novel in vitro enzyme assays on our proprietary microfluidic platform, and manage external collaborations. This role will combine hands-on wet-bench biochemistry, data generation and analysis on Velocity’s high-throughput platform, as well as leadership by managing internal and external projects. As an early hire, you’ll have significant opportunity to work with the founding team and shape the scientific direction and culture of Velocity.

This Role Will Involve

  • Designing, performing, and analyzing high-throughput enzyme assays on Velocity’s platform

  • Designing and managing large-scale internal/external data generation campaigns

  • Developing new high-throughput classical quantitative biochemical assays

  • Working closely with AI/ML engineers to guide model development and evaluations

  • Shaping Velocity’s scientific roadmap alongside the founding team

Required Qualifications

  • PhD in life sciences (Biochemistry, Biophysics, Chemical Biology, or Structural Biology preferred)

  • 3+ years of relevant industry experience

  • Expertise in enzymology and in vitro functional assays

  • Deep understanding of protein structure and function

  • Fluent in common molecular biology techniques (construct design, cloning, DNA and protein purification, etc.)

  • Fluent in Python programming

  • Ability to move quickly between strategic planning and hands-on execution

  • Exceptional scientific rigor and attention to detail

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading large-scale internal/external projects

  • Hands-on experience performing other protein biophysical assays characterizing stability, binding, etc.

  • Experience performing recombinant protein expression and purification

  • Experience with NGS workflows

This position might be a good fit if you…

  • Are passionate about working on problems with huge potential to improve human health

  • Enjoy rigorous science and designing and performing complex biophysical experiments

  • Are excited to shape an early startup and influence how we work and what we build

  • Are highly organized and a self-directed learner

  • Want to join a fast-paced, collaborative environment in the heart of the Bay Area

Benefits

  • Competitive salary and equity

  • Full health, dental, and vision insurance

  • 401(k) plan

Location

  • In-person; MBC BioLabs in San Carlos, CA

  • On-site parking available

  • 10-minute walk from a Caltrain station

jobs.title: Founding Product Implementation Lead
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Paxos Health is a Seed-stage healthcare AI startup that has raised >$7M in venture capital funding, with a product already operating in production with customers. Our founding team comes from Stanford, Meta, Microsoft, Medtronic, Columbia, University of Waterloo, and has founded previous startups and healthcare nonprofits.

We are building the AI-native operating system for getting patients access to the medical technologies their doctors prescribe. Too often, even when a physician decides a patient needs a healthcare product (heart valves, cancer tests, genetic diagnostics, prosthetics, neurostimulation devices, home medical equipment, etc.), health insurance companies deny coverage, and breakthrough technologies struggle to reach the people they were built to help.

We help healthcare manufacturers fight for coverage patient-by-patient. Before LLMs, this work was too difficult to use AI technology for, and human teams were forced to cut corners to get through all of the patient cases. But now, AI can help manufacturers meet increasingly complex insurer requirements and get more patients access to care.

About the role

Paxos Health is looking for a hands-on Founding Product Implementation Lead. As our first business hire, reporting directly to the CEO, you'll own the product and implementation work that gets customers live on our platform and help shape how our product evolves.

Most of your time will go to customer implementation, where you'll be the bridge between our customers and our technical team. You won't build the product AI workflows or software yourself, but you'll understand AI well enough to know what's possible, spot gaps, and judge whether outputs meet customer needs. The rest of your time goes into bringing what you learn across customers back into our product.

This is a doer's role with real ownership. As we grow, you'll have opportunities to build out our implementation and customer success team, or help establish our product function.

You can expect a fast-paced, intense, and dynamic working environment where everyone has strategic ownership. We are a small team where everyone works directly with the founders. We take our work seriously, but we don’t take ourselves too seriously, and we are building a culture that prioritizes constant learning and feedback.

Responsibilities

  • Lead customer implementations end to end, diving deep into each customer's workflows, templates, and past cases to translate their needs into precise product requirements and specs for engineering, including expected outputs, business rules, and edge cases.

  • Test AI outputs against real customer cases and confirm workflows meet customer needs before go-live.

  • Serve as the customer's main point of contact through go-live and beyond, tracking adoption and flagging issues early.

  • Build playbooks, templates, and automation so every customer goes live faster than the last, and bring customer insights back to the team to make our platform more configurable.

  • Help run patient-facing programs, including portal setup, intake automations, and patient communications.

Requirements

  • 3-5+ years of hands-on experience in implementation, product, solutions, consulting, customer success, engineering, or a similar role, ideally including time at a startup.

  • Strong technical aptitude and hands-on AI fluency. You pick up new tools quickly, use AI to get real work done (including building your own workflows), and can judge whether AI outputs are good enough to trust.

  • Confidence leading working sessions with senior customer stakeholders and translating product requirements and timelines between customers and engineers.

  • Proven ability to juggle many workstreams without dropping balls.

  • A bias toward rolling up your sleeves and doing the work yourself, with the judgment to own customer relationships with minimal oversight.

  • Able to work in person in New York.

Nice to have

  • A technical background, such as a computer science or engineering degree, or prior experience as an engineer, technical PM, or solutions engineer.

  • Healthcare experience

  • Customer-facing experience at a B2B company, such as implementation, solutions, or customer success.

  • Familiarity with HIPAA and SOC 2.

  • Experience as an early employee at a startup.

In your first 90 days

Here's what success looks like as you ramp up. The specifics will flex with our customer pipeline and your strengths.

Days 1 to 30: Learn the business and our customers

  • Shadow live implementations with our CEO and technical team, learn our product and the patient access process, and meet our customers' patient access and reimbursement teams.

Days 31 to 60: Own your first implementation

  • Lead implementation for a new medtech or diagnostics customer, from mapping their workflows and collecting templates and past cases to writing product requirements and testing AI outputs before go-live.

Days 61 to 90: Make it repeatable

  • Take that customer live as their main point of contact, and turn what you learned into the first version of our implementation playbook.

By day 90, you'll be leading and running implementations on your own, have a playbook the team uses, and be the person our CEO trusts to own a growing share of our customer and product work.

Compensation

  • $120-160k USD base salary, calibrated to candidate’s background and level of experience

  • Very generous equity package, reflecting our belief that the high ownership given to our early team should come with meaningful upside

  • We offer health, dental, and vision insurance, plus standard paid time off per early-stage startup norms

jobs.title: People Operations Manager - NeuroNav
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Hours: Part-time, 20 hours per week

Location: Remote, United States


Do you love building the people side of a mission-driven company — where new hires feel welcome, the details run smoothly, and the team feels cared for? Join us as our People Operations Manager and help the people who help families thrive.

About NeuroNav

At NeuroNav, we believe everyone deserves the opportunity to make their own choices and shape their story, regardless of disability. Our mission is to enhance the quality of life for adults with developmental disabilities through simplicity and choice. We help families navigate California’s Self-Determination Program, and our team of Navigators is the heart and soul of that work.

Founded at Stanford in 2020, we’re a high-growth, innovative team, and we’re building the people practices to match. Behind every Navigator supporting a family is a team that deserves to feel supported too. That’s where you come in.

About the Role

As our People Operations Manager, you’ll be the HR expert and steady hand behind the employee experience. You’ll make sure every new hire feels prepared and welcome from day one, keep payroll, compliance, and our people systems running with care, and oversee the IT that helps our team do their best work. You’ll also bring our culture to life through the rituals and moments that keep people excited to stay.

You’ll partner closely with our part-time Recruiter, who owns hiring, and you’ll be their manager and thought partner. Together, you’ll make sure a great candidate becomes a well-supported teammate.

This is a hands-on role with real ownership, clear priorities, and room to grow as we grow.

Responsibilities Include

HR Operations, Payroll & Compliance

You’ll be the trusted go-to for how we do HR well.

  • Bring HR best practices to our policies, processes, and everyday employee questions

  • Keep employee records and HR systems (Gusto and related tools) accurate and organized

  • Oversee payroll: from timesheet approvals and error follow-up through final submission

  • Stay on top of compliance mail and filings, including state tax letters, agency follow-up, forms, and audits

  • Answer questions on HR policies, benefits, time off, and Gusto settings

  • Maintain clear people documentation and build an employee-friendly people ops FAQ

Onboarding & Offboarding

You’ll shape the first impression, and the last one, for every teammate.

  • Draft and manage offer letters, legal documents, and signatures once a candidate says yes

  • Run onboarding through Gusto and stay in touch with new hires until day one and beyond

  • Make sure every new hire has their accounts, equipment, and a warm welcome

  • Handle offboarding with care: access removal, separation agreements, final pay, and severance where applicable

  • Work hand in hand with our Recruiter for a seamless handoff from accepted offer to start date

IT & Systems Oversight

You’ll keep our tools, systems, and IT support running smoothly so our team can focus on families.

  • Oversee our outsourced IT firm, serving as the primary point of contact and ensuring timely, high-quality support for the team.

  • Monitor the IT firm's performance, follow up on open issues, and ensure service levels and team needs are being met.

  • Identify opportunities to simplify our tools, improve IT processes, and streamline onboarding and offboarding.

Culture, Engagement & Retention

You’ll help make NeuroNav a place people thrive and retain our amazing talent.

  • Plan, attend, and organize our company offsite

  • Coordinate town halls and internal communications

  • Organize monthly team lunches and other morale-building moments

  • Support rituals, recognition, and values-in-action

  • Listen for themes in the employee experience and share what you learn with leadership

Compensation & People Programs

You’ll help us build programs that are fair, thoughtful, and well documented.

  • Research and benchmark compensation

  • Support role changes, leveling, and comp documentation

  • Help run performance reviews and comp cycles

Compensation strategy and final decisions rest with leadership. You’ll bring the analysis and make it happen.

Team Leadership & Operations

You’ll help our small, mighty team stay organized and supported.

  • Manage and coach our part-time Recruiter through regular 1:1s and shared priorities

  • Work with the Recruiter and leadership so hiring plans flow smoothly into onboarding

  • Contribute to special projects tied to employee experience, internal communication, or HR tooling

Recruiting is run day to day by our Recruiter; final hiring decisions rest with leadership.

What You’ll Bring

  • 5+ years of hands-on HR or people operations experience, ideally as a generalist in a small or growing organization

  • Working knowledge of US and California employment compliance and payroll, including state tax notices and filings

  • Experience with HRIS and payroll platforms (Gusto or similar)

  • Comfort administering SaaS tools and working with vendors, such as Google Workspace, Slack, HubSpot, and Notion

  • Experience with compensation benchmarking and leveling

  • Experience managing, mentoring, or coordinating the work of others

  • Warm, clear communication and comfort working across roles, schedules, and time zones

  • Alignment with our mission and values, and a proactive, organized, thoughtful approach

  • Comfort owning ambiguity and building from scratch

  • Nice to have: HR certification (SHRM-CP, PHR, or similar); experience in a nonprofit, healthcare, or disability-services setting

What Success Looks Like

  • New hires feel prepared, welcomed, and supported from day one

  • Payroll, compliance, and records are accurate, timely, and well documented

  • Our tools are clean, secure, and cost-conscious

  • Culture moments are consistent, thoughtful, and rooted in our values

  • Our Recruiter feels supported and hiring flows smoothly into onboarding

  • Leadership trusts that our people are in caring, capable hands

Benefits

We believe in supporting our employees’ well-being and work-life balance as part of our culture.

  • Remote first: ability to work from home

  • Paid time off

  • Sick or flex days

  • Annual company retreat

Pay: $38–$45 per hour (depending on experience)

All official hiring communication comes only from @neuronav.org.

 - Support rituals, recognition, and values-in-action

 - Listen for themes in the employee experience and share what you learn with leadership
   


COMPENSATION & PEOPLE PROGRAMS

You’ll help us build programs that are fair, thoughtful, and well documented.

 - Research and benchmark compensation

 - Support role changes, leveling, and comp documentation

 - Help run performance reviews and comp cycles

Compensation strategy and final decisions rest with leadership. You’ll bring the analysis and make it happen.



TEAM LEADERSHIP & OPERATIONS

You’ll help our small, mighty team stay organized and supported.

 - Manage and coach our part-time Recruiter through regular 1:1s and shared priorities

 - Work with the Recruiter and leadership so hiring plans flow smoothly into onboarding

 - Contribute to special projects tied to employee experience, internal communication, or HR tooling

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 5+ years of hands-on HR or people operations experience, ideally as a generalist in a small or growing organization

 - Working knowledge of US and California employment compliance and payroll, including state tax notices and filings

 - Experience with HRIS and payroll platforms (Gusto or similar)

 - Comfort administering SaaS tools and working with vendors, such as Google Workspace, Slack, HubSpot, and Notion

 - Experience with compensation benchmarking and leveling

 - Experience managing, mentoring, or coordinating the work of others

 - Warm, clear communication and comfort working across roles, schedules, and time zones

 - Alignment with our mission and values, and a proactive, organized, thoughtful approach

 - Comfort owning ambiguity and building from scratch

 - Nice to have: HR certification (SHRM-CP, PHR, or similar); experience in a nonprofit, healthcare, or disability-services setting




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - New hires feel prepared, welcomed, and supported from day one

 - Payroll, compliance, and records are accurate, timely, and well documented

 - Our tools are clean, secure, and cost-conscious

 - Culture moments are consistent, thoughtful, and rooted in our values

 - Our Recruiter feels supported and hiring flows smoothly into onboarding

 - Leadership trusts that our people are in caring, capable hands




BENEFITS

We believe in supporting our employees’ well-being and work-life balance as part of our culture. 

 - Remote first: ability to work from home

 - Paid time off

 - Sick or flex days

 - Annual company retreat

Pay: $38–$45 per hour (depending on experience)

jobs.title: Head / Director of Marketing
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Head / Director of Marketing

About Endless Commerce

Endless Commerce is an AI-powered CommerceOS that helps consumer brands manage the chaos of omnichannel operations. We serve brands scaling from $5M to $100M+ in revenue, providing real-time inventory visibility, EDI and purchase order automation, and supply chain intelligence across DTC, wholesale, marketplaces, and retail channels.

Our clients include brands like EADEM, Great Jones, Heyday, Tin Can, Pattern Brands and more. We are a lean, scrappy operator team and we are moving fast.

The Role

You lead marketing at Endless. You set our marketing strategy and manage the team that carries it out.

We're looking for someone plugged into the consumer brand world, with a clear view of how to make Endless the name operators know. We move fast and work closely together. You'll do well here if you like being in the strategy and the execution, and if this industry gets you excited.

What Success Looks Like

  • Trade shows. Show season starts in February, so this is your first priority. Endless should get noticed at every show we attend.

  • Brand recognition. Consumer brands recognize Endless online and when there’s conversation about scaling omnichannel brands into new doors, EDI, ERPs, just-in-time-inventory, Endless is always at the heart of it.

  • Working with our media platform. Commerce is Chaos, Sam Rose's media property, has its own executive producer and editor. Collaborate with them on where Endless shows up there, such as ads in the newsletter or on YouTube.

  • Better strategy and organization for our fast-moving team. Moving fast means even folks with the best intentions can get overwhelmed or disorganized— drive strategy and keep our ducks in a row so that we can be a focused, productive team even when there are shiny new objects to get excited about.

What You'll Own

  • Marketing strategy. Channel mix and campaign plan across LinkedIn, email, paid and events.

  • Managing a team. Work closely with our Marketing Manager, plus freelance video and copywriting support.

  • Managing our fractional paid media resource and owning the paid budget.

  • Events and trade shows. You pick the shows and build the budget. The whole team works events, and you're accountable for how they go and the integrated online/offline strategy.

  • Commerce is Chaos. Collaborate with the executive producer and editor of Commerce is Chaos, Sam Rose's media property, on when and how Endless is featured.

  • Attribution and reporting. You own how we measure marketing, so we know what each channel produces and what it costs us to acquire a customer.

  • Messaging. You turn what converts into positioning.

You're a Great Fit If

  • You've led marketing for a team before and set its strategy

  • You've managed people

  • You know the consumer brand industry and have a strong point of view on how to stand out in it as a B2B SaaS business in the operations space

  • You enjoy both strategy and execution

  • You like moving fast with a small team

Logistics

  • Title: Head of Marketing or Director of Marketing (to decide)

  • Reports to: Sam Rose, CEO

  • Full-time, remote

  • Full benefits package including healthcare and 401k

  • Compensation: $150,000–$175,000 base

jobs.title: Founding Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
curl -s jobs.blueberrysocial.com | jq

About us

Blueberry is building the autonomous 1:1 marketer. Our AI enables brands to drive personalized conversations with every customer, supercharge lifecycle marketing outcomes, and drive revenue.

We’re:

  • Enterprise-proven: Trusted by the Fortune 500, San Francisco 49ers, and DTC brands generating $100M+ in annual sales.

  • Growing quickly: In six months, continuously doubled revenue and customers onboarded.

  • Talent-Dense: 7 people, 75% ex-founders

  • Early: The operating systems, playbooks, and leadership team that scale Blueberry are still being built.

AI is changing how every consumer brand communicates with its customers. We are defining that shift—and we’re looking for someone who wants their fingerprints on the company and category we build.

The Role

Brands with millions of followers rely on Blueberry to authentically engage their customers at scale. As our Founding Engineer, you’ll be a co-architect of everything we build at Blueberry. You’ll be responsible for shaping the technical foundation of the company: product, platform, and team culture.

You’ll work directly with the founders and founding engineering team to:

  • Build and scale the core product that enables brands to authentically engage millions of followers.

  • Make foundational architecture and stack decisions that allow us to move fast today while preparing for global scale tomorrow.

  • Translate customer needs into elegant, resilient technical systems that balance speed, quality, and reliability.

  • Set the tone for our engineering culture — one that is high-caliber, collaborative, and deeply product-minded.

You’ll have massive influence over how Blueberry evolves, from the codebase to the customer experience to the engineering org itself.

Tech Stack: Convex, Next.js, AI SDK, and more

What You’ll Do

  • Build customer-facing features end-to-end that directly impact how brands engage their followers, from requirements through launch.

  • Turn real customer feedback and usage data into product improvements that feel intuitive and reliable.

  • Collaborate deeply with design to translate flows and interactions into well engineered solutions.

  • Prototype quickly, ship often, and iterate based on usage and metrics.

  • Maintain and improve code quality, tooling, and test coverage so the product remains reliable as we scale.

  • Build, monitor, and improve operational telemetry and observability for user flows that matter.

  • Work across the stack with a focus on delivering delightful user experiences while balancing performance and scalability.

  • Contribute to technical standards and practices that help the engineering team move fast with confidence.

  • Participate in architectural discussions that will influence how the system scales and performs.

Who You Are

  • A full stack engineer with 3 plus years of professional experience building SaaS, AI enabled, or consumer applications.

  • Comfortable moving fast in an early stage environment and shipping features that land in the hands of real customers.

  • You take initiative and care deeply about the quality of your work.

  • You do not just point out problems, you roll up your sleeves and solve them.

  • You hold yourself to a high bar and look for clean, maintainable solutions.

  • You bring a clear point of view on what excellent code and product experience looks like while staying collaborative and low ego.

  • Entrepreneurial by nature, you thrive in ambiguity and enjoy shaping product from the ground up.

  • You want to build with others who share the same high standards and ownership mindset.

  • Familiarity with AI or large language model powered products.

  • Background building consumer facing products, personalization engines, or customer data systems.

  • Previous early stage startup or founding team experience.

  • Experience with social media APIs such as Instagram, TikTok, or Meta.

  • Experience writing infrastructure for observability, performance monitoring, or alerting.

Why Join Us

  • Own meaningful product early. You will ship features used by real customers from day one and directly shape how brands engage millions of followers.

  • Founding-level influence. You will help define product direction, engineering standards, and how the team builds while decisions are still lightweight and impact is high.

  • Product-driven culture. Engineers work closely with design, founders, and customers, with decisions grounded in real usage and outcomes.

  • Momentum with substance. Live customers, early revenue, and strong investor backing mean you are joining at a moment where great execution compounds fast.

What We Offer:

  • Office in SF: We believe the best work is done in person. We cover lunch everyday in our office, and dinner for days you work late.

  • Team Outings: We believe that world-class companies are built by world-class people, so you can expect team dinners, escape rooms, and yes, NFL games

  • Benefits: Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance with 401(k) matching, Unlimited PTO

  • Build the future of how brands interact with consumers, authentically

  • An opportunity to lead and define our company and industry.

Want to help shape how the fastest growing brands connect with their customers? We’d love to meet you.

Blueberry is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, color, age, national origin, religion, physical and mental disability, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity/assignment, citizenship, pregnancy or maternity, protected veteran status, or any other status prohibited by applicable national, federal, state or local law.

jobs.title: Partnerships & Community Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Endless Commerce

Endless Commerce is an AI-powered CommerceOS that helps consumer brands manage the chaos of omnichannel operations. We serve brands scaling from $5M to $100M+ in revenue, providing real-time inventory visibility, EDI and purchase order automation, and supply chain intelligence across DTC, wholesale, marketplaces, and retail channels.

Our clients include brands like EADEM, Great Jones, Heyday, Tin Can, Pattern Brands and more. We are a lean, scrappy operator team and we are moving fast.

The Role

You're responsible for making sure Endless is part of the conversation whenever consumer brand operators talk shop. That means working closely with companies that serve the same brands we do, from fractional ops agencies to other SaaS businesses, and helping lead our referral partnerships.

You'll make sure we show up in the right Reddit threads and Slack groups. And you'll build the relationships that put Endless at the heart of conversations about ops, EDI, ERPs, inventory and order management, and just-in-time inventory. This is a very public, external facing role and the right candidate is ready to represent a growing start-up online and in-person.

What You'll Own

  • Referral partnerships. Build and run our referral program with 3PLs, logistics providers, agencies, supply chain consultants and SaaS companies that serve our ICP. Keep in regular touch with partners and keep partner records current.

  • Referring out. When a client needs something we don't do, connect them with the right partner. Partners who get business from us send business back. You connect the dots on who might be a fit for who, which means staying close to our sales and operations teams.

  • Fractional operators. Build direct relationships with fractional ops leaders and agencies, both as partners and as a sales channel.

  • Customer referrals. Build a program that brings in one new customer for each existing customer.

  • Community. Show up where consumer operators talk, including Reddit, Slack groups and social, so Endless and our exec team stay part of those conversations.

  • Events. Work trade shows with the team, from prep to the show floor to follow-up, and decide what each new contact hears from us next.

You're a Great Fit If

  • You have 3–10 years of partnerships, community, lifecycle, client services and/or marketing operations experience

  • You love talking to people and remember names, faces and who needs what

  • You take ownership of relationships and don't wait for permission to run with them

  • You know when to automate and when a personal touch is worth the extra effort

  • You're organized and process-oriented, and creative in how you engage partners

  • You're hands-on: you write the emails, build the campaigns and run the day-to-day

Logistics

  • Reports to: Sam Rose, CEO

  • Full-time, remote with moderate business travel

  • Full benefits package including healthcare and 401k

  • Compensation: $120,000–$150,000

jobs.title: Founder's Office, Customer Success (New york)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Optexity

Optexity is a product-driven research lab building clinical reasoning and computer use models on data no other lab can reach. We deploy directly inside clinics and hospitals — including systems with no APIs, using integration infrastructure we've built and open-sourced — and in return become their preferred partner. That gives us proprietary clinical reasoning trajectories from practicing physicians, and a feedback loop between real patient encounters, our models, and the products built on top of them.

We're a small, fast-moving founding team with multiple published papers in NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR etc and background from Apple, Amazon, Microsoft, CMU, IIT.

We are backed by world-class investors and leaders like Jeff Dean, Neotribe VC, PearVC, Together Fund and Zapier Fund.

 

How we work

  • Customer obsession — we start with the customer and work backwards

  • Intellectual honesty — ideas matter more than titles; we communicate directly and assume good intent, even in disagreement

  • Bias for action — we build and learn with customers rather than debate in the abstract

  • Extreme ownership — we own outcomes, not just tasks, and see problems through

About the role

This is not a support role, and not a sales role. It is a flexible, hands-on role for someone who wants to start a company one day. You will be the face of Optexity to our customers: the practices, clinics and doctors who use our product every day. You will sit with them on site, learn how they work, and bring what you learn back to the founders to shape the product. In one role you get product, customer discovery, customer success, customer coordination and a taste of engineering.

This role is on site in New York, where all of our customers are.

What you’ll do

  • Work directly with doctors, practice managers and clinic staff to understand their workflows and pain points

  • Run customer discovery: gather requirements, spot patterns across practices, and turn them into clear product priorities

  • Help design the product with the founders and engineers, and test new features with customers

  • Onboard new practices: coordinate setup, access, integrations and training

  • Drive usage: track adoption, find out why users stall, and get more doctors using the product more often

  • Be the single point of contact for customers, and close the loop on every issue and request

  • Work with engineers to debug problems, write specs, and ship small fixes yourself where you can

  • Help with early sales and renewals by building trust and relationships with practices

Ideal candidate

  • Genuinely wants to start a company someday and wants a front-row seat

  • Strong communicator who is comfortable talking with doctors and busy clinic staff

  • Highly organized, follows through, and closes loops

  • Energized by ambiguity and takes ownership without needing to be guided

  • Based in New York, or willing to move, and comfortable being on site with customers most days

  • Comfortable with technology, and curious about how software gets built

  • New Grads welcome to apply

Nice to have

  • Prior experience in customer success, consulting, startups, product or operations

  • Familiarity with healthcare, practice operations or EMR systems

  • Basic technical skills such as SQL, scripting or working with APIs

  • Prior founder or founding team experience

What you get

  • Direct, daily work with the founders, plus exposure to board and investor conversations

  • A broad view of product, customers, sales and engineering that few roles offer

  • Real ownership, with scope that grows as the company does

  • Support on your path to starting your own company

  • Competitive salary
